projects.author: TonyChen56
projects.summary: 阮老师好，我做了一个参考文献核验工具 Reference Checker，想自荐给科技爱好者周刊。 网站地址： 中文界面： 解决什么问题 论文中的参考文献即使格式正确、DOI 能打开，也可能对应另一篇文章。使用 ChatGPT 等工具辅助写作后，逐条确认文献是否存在、作者和标题是否一致，也是一件费时的事。 Reference Checker 可以检查整份参考文献列表，找到匹配的出版记录，并把原始引用与来源信息并排展示，方便学生、研究者、教师和编辑核对。 主要功能 批量导入： 直接粘贴参考文献，或登录后从 PDF、Word、BibTeX、RIS 等 14 种格式及 arXiv 论文导入；单次导入最多 500 条。 核对真实来源： 按标识符和学科检索 Crossref、OpenAlex、PubMed 等 12 个学术数据源中的相关记录，每条结果显示实际查询的来源和可访问的出版链接。 逐字段检查： 比较标题、作者、年份、期刊、DOI 等信息，识别“有效 DOI 指向错误论文”、重复引用和元数据不一致等情况。 修改与导出： 提供 APA、MLA、Chicago、Harvard、Vancouver、IEEE、ABNT 七种引用格式的修正建议，支持 Markdown、CSV、JSON、BibTeX、RIS 导出；登录后还可保存历史记录和分享报告。 免费使用 访客无需注册，每天可检查 100 条粘贴的参考文献；登录后每天有 500 条核验额度，并可使用文件导入、导出、历史记录和分享功能。无需购买或订阅。界面支持中文、英文等六种语言。 使用边界 工具核对的是文献来源及引用信息，不判断论文中的论点是否得到该文献支持。未找到匹配记录不等于文献伪造，也不能证明使用了 AI。PDF 导入需要可选中的文字，扫描件需先做 OCR；目前每次处理一份参考文献列表。 界面示例 下图展示逐字段核对的工作区：示例引用的 DOI 指向另一篇论文，工具保留原始引用并显示对应来源信息。 欢迎试用并提出建议，谢谢！

projects.title: Show HN: Wick, a daily word game where you guess by meaning, not spelling
projects.author: jpage2
projects.summary: Hello HN! This is the first game I've ever made and I've been hooked on making apps/web apps ever since. At first it was closed-source for the first couple months of its launch, but this week I decided it should be made open-source. My reasoning for this is there are already a lot of games similar to mine that are about guessing a word based on the meaning of the word and narrowing down the secret word; but I added a little twist. The game, "Wick", allows you to both narrow down the word by either 1. Guessing by meaning of the word like "fruit" is hot if the word is "lemon", or 2. Asking questions like "Is it a type of fruit?" and the Keeper will answer "Yes/No/Not Sure" etc... but will never spoil the answer. It works by turning words into an embedding, which in simpler terms is a list of numbers that capture how the word is used semantically. Words used in similar ways get similar numbers. It comes from Gemini's embedding API for web/live race mode, but for iOS single player it uses free apple-intelligence on-device for the questions and it uses Apple's built-in English embedding and four small Core ML models for other languages like Spanish, German, Italian, and French. The closeness of words is based on cosine similarity of two embeddings. The server embeds a vocabulary of 9,850 common words once, sorts them by closeness to the day's secret, and your guess is how close it is to rank 1 (the secret word). Rank 2 would be the closest word to the secret word. The categories of closeness are based on temperature so it goes: boiling, hot, warm, cool, cold, and freezing. At the end of the solve/game, you are rewarded with a semantic meaning map where it shows you all of your guesses and where they landed relative to the secret word as you narrowed in on it or gave up. There's also no accounts at all, no ads, and no tracking of course. I pay out of pocket and am hoping to get users before I monetize or try to make money off the website. Right now I'm just hosting it for fun. I can do this because the vocabulary gets cached and there's only one embedding call per guess. It's one developer working on this app and web app. I'm receiving no funding currently for developing the game. I wanted to copy osu!'s playbook a little, mostly because it's difficult for any game to maintain a moat or advantage over incumbents and have a reason to retain users. I thought that making it open-source and allowing people to contribute and add their own taste to the game would be nice. Also, I just enjoy making open-source code recently. Play a few rounds please and let me know what you think or if you have any critiques to make it more fun/modular! I'd really like contributions if you're feeling up to it or comments/feedback on how I can improve! Play it Live with no App Required: https://guesswick.com/ Source Code: https://github.com/jasonepage/Wick iOS listing: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6777743483

projects.author: IllegalCreed

github.name: IllegalCreed/algorithms-visualization
github.description: 92 个数据结构与算法的逐步动画，四语言代码逐行同步高亮 · Step-through animations for 92 data structures & algorithms

projects.summary: 一个交互式的数据结构与算法可视化网站，9 大类 92 个条目。其中 77 个算法可以单步前进、后退、拖动进度条，动画旁边的 TypeScript / Python / Go / Rust 代码会随步骤高亮当前执行的行，同时显示变量和每一步的解说；另外 15 个数据结构页可以直接操作。适合刷题、准备面试和课堂演示，也可以当作 Vue 3 项目来看可视化代码怎么组织。 亮点 每个算法先生成一整串步骤快照，播放器只负责回放，所以能后退、跳到任意一步，倍速 0.5×–3×，还能循环播放，键盘 ← → 空格都能操作。 同一步在四种语言里各自高亮对应的行，旁边是变量面板和一句话解说。 12 个排序模块可以输入自己的数组，输入会写进地址栏的 ?input=，把链接发给别人就是同一组数据。 二分查找和快速排序两页会在关键步骤停下来出题。 除了常见面试题，还有 2-SAT、最大流、后缀数组、AC 自动机、FFT、Pollard's Rho、扫描线求交、换根 DP 这些进阶主题。 中英双语，手机上也能用。纯前端，运行时只依赖 Vue / Vue Router / Pinia 和 Shiki，没有 UI 库和图表库，MIT 协议。 和同类项目比：VisuAlgo 的自定义输入和训练系统更成熟，Hello 算法的内容更成体系；这个项目的特点是把讲解、逐步动画和多语言逐行代码放在同一页里。

projects.author: shbernal

github.name: shbernal/pptx-ts
github.description: Create PowerPoint presentations from TypeScript

projects.summary: pptx-ts 是一个用 TypeScript 生成 PowerPoint（.pptx）文件的库，适合根据会变化的数据批量生成幻灯片，比如月报、每个客户一份的报告，或网页上的“下载 PPT”按钮。生成过程不需要运行 PowerPoint 或安装 Office，可在 Node.js 和浏览器中使用。它还能打开已有的 .pptx：查看内容、修改后保存，或把整份演示文稿反向转换成 TypeScript 代码。 亮点 功能全面：文本、可自动跨页的表格、形状、连接线、图片、SVG、音视频；原生图表内嵌 Excel 工作簿，在 PowerPoint 里可以直接“编辑数据”；还支持母版与版式、分节、演讲者备注、渐变、LaTeX 公式和 3D 模型。 能读也能写：pptx-ts/inspect 快速查看文件内容，pptx-ts/read 修改已有文件且未改动的部分保持原样，pptx-ts/script 把演示文稿转换成能重建它的 TypeScript 代码。在 PowerPoint 里手工做一页，再看生成的代码，是学习 API 最快的方式。 与 PptxGenJS 的区别：pptx-ts 源自 PptxGenJS v4.0.1 并独立发展。用同样 22 种幻灯片场景对比，pptx-ts 生成了其中 21 种，PptxGenJS 生成了 10 种；pptx-ts 的 21 份文件全部通过 Open XML SDK 校验无错误。PptxGenJS 只能写入，不能读取或编辑已有文件。 HTML 的 可以直接转换成分页的幻灯片；文本框可按真实字体度量自动缩放，在写入文件前就确定排版。 Node.js 24 可直接运行 .mts 文件，无需构建步骤；MIT 协议，有完整的文档站：

projects.title: Show HN: Client-side image cropping for any file input, without coding
projects.author: rikschennink
projects.summary: Hi HN! We built CropGuide for people who don't code (or use platforms that don't allow custom code) but do want to improve the quality of images uploaded by their users. To make that possible, we've built an admin tool where you configure your image requirements. Then you add a script tag to the page with the file upload field, either a standard file input or something more exotic powered by a library, and that's it. The script catches images before they're added to the file input and lets the user edit them. Once edited, CropGuide places the resulting image back in the file input and everything continues as normal. We really wanted to stay away from storing or processing images on our servers, so all of this happens client-side. Only the image requirements are fetched from the server. Of course we're sharing because we're excited about having built and launched something new. Now it's fingers crossed that we can get some traction. Would love to hear what you think!

projects.title: OhMyGame 开源 10 天拿到 936 个 star 的一个小复盘
projects.author: dihuanginfo
projects.summary: 我们团队最近开源了一个 AI 游戏创作工具 [OhMyGame]( https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame)，主打“开源的一人 AI 游戏工作室”：用户描述自己的想法，Agent 完成游戏设计、生成资产，再进行开发和测试。 我们把 Canvas 和游戏工作流整合在一起，希望让素材生成、编辑和游戏开发的过程更直观。 ![OhMyGame 首页]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-home-overview.jpg) 我们是一个不自带流量的小团队。开源前 10 天，项目拿到了 936 个 star 。想把这段时间的数字、流量来源和用户反馈分享一下，也想请教大家：发布最初一波热度过去后，怎么继续让项目被需要它的人看到？ ## 先说数字 这 10 天里： - 936 个 star ，113 个 fork 。 - 发布了 11 个版本，从 beta.3 到 beta.4.9 。 - 合并了 131 个 PR 。 - 用户提了 36 个 issue ，已经关闭了 26 个。 - 没有投流，主要靠 X 上的内容传播。 下面是这段时间的 star 增长曲线： ![OhMyGame 开源前 10 天的 Star 增长曲线]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-star-history.webp) [查看增长曲线动画]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-star-history.mp4) ## 关注从哪里来？ 我看了 GitHub 的仓库访问数据，这 10 天总共有 3,648 位访客。前五个访问来源分别是： - X：1,194 位访客。 - GitHub 站内：359 位访客。 - 官网 ohmygame.ai：326 位访客。 - Google：208 位访客。 - V2EX：138 位访客。 X 一个渠道带来的访客，比后面四个来源加起来还多，占这五个来源合计的约 54%。 这里统计的是仓库访客来源，不是各渠道带来的 star 数，也不是全部访客的来源占比。 比较明显的两次增长，分别发生在两条 X 帖子传播之后。 **第一次是开源首发帖。** 开源当晚 11 点多，团队成员 Dogxi 发了项目介绍，目前有约 3 万次浏览。 刚发出时没什么动静，第二天早上 7 点左右才开始明显增长，到傍晚新增了大约 300 个 star 。 ![Dogxi 在 X 上发布的首发帖]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-x-launch-post.webp) **第二次是 Hyper3D 合作帖。** 10 月 10 日晚上，我发了介绍 Hyper3D 合作的帖子，目前有约 2.2 万次浏览。帖子点赞持续增加，第二天仓库又增长了约 180 个 star 。 ![Hyper3D 合作帖]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-x-hyper3d-post.webp) 不过，到了 16 号以后，增长就慢下来了，三天涨了 48 个。 这次比较直接的感受是：至少对我们这个项目来说，外部内容传播带来的关注很明显，GitHub 站内也有流量，但没有自动带来持续增长。 ## 这 10 天，我们怎么回应用户反馈？ 我们尽量第一时间回复用户，并尽快修复问题、补上需要的功能。举三个具体例子： **1. 简体中文界面** 有人提出需要简体中文界面，3 天后就在 beta.4.7 中上线了。 对应 issue： https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues/134 **2. 撤回 Agent 的一轮操作** 有人希望 Agent 改坏了之后能退回去。 4 天后发布的 beta.4.9 支持了这个功能：Agent 每轮操作后会列出修改过的文件，用户可以一键撤回。 对应 issue： https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues/202 **3. Windows 上的 bug** 有人报告示例项目在 Windows 上没法 remix ，37 分钟后修复就合并了，当天随 beta.4.2 发了出去。 对应 issue： https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues/122 目前我们很大一部分开发工作，就是围绕这些真实反馈展开的。 ## 用户已经做出了什么？ 贴几个用户作品。下面的图片可以点击，打开对应的实机录屏。 **Hunter Space：低多边形风格的 3D 野外探索** [![Hunter Space]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-user-hunter-space.webp)]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-user-hunter-space.mp4) **Windmere Highlands：在高地草甸和石阵间奔跑** [![Windmere Highlands]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-user-windmere-highlands.webp)]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-user-windmere-highlands.mp4) **第一人称恐怖走廊，Backrooms 风格** [![Backrooms 风格恐怖走廊]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-user-backrooms.webp)]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-user-backrooms.mp4) **2D 弓箭手放置游戏，带技能树和掉落** [![2D 弓箭手放置游戏]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-user-archer.webp)]( https://www.dihuang.me/assets/blog/ohmygame-user-archer.mp4) ## 为什么做这个？ 我自己是 3D 视觉和图形学出身，一直想做和游戏有关的事。 做了前面几个应用之后，我越来越觉得，还是要做自己有感觉的东西。否则遇到困难时，很难一直坚持下去。 选择开源，也是希望大家能用更便宜、更简单的方式创造游戏，和用户一起把工具慢慢做好。 感谢给项目点 star 、提交 issue 和 PR 的朋友，也感谢 Hyper3D 提供赞助，让用户能体验到 3D 生成能力。 ## 接下来 近期我们在研究直接接入 Codex 和 Claude Code 的 CLI ，也会完善互动叙事和插件相关的支持。 更长期还想支持多人游戏、Unity 、Unreal ，以及更多创作工作流。这些还在计划中，需要一步步做。 - GitHub： https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame - 官网： https://ohmygame.ai - 完整博客： https://www.dihuang.me/blog/ohmygame-10-days

Cursor 中文完全教程 AI 编程工具 Cursor 的中文上手手册，10 大章节：安装、Tab 补全、Chat、Agent、Rules 规则文件、MCP、模型配置、真实工作流、快捷键、常见坑。全原创中文，示例可直接照做，适合刚接触 AI 编程编辑器的人。 2. AI 产品经理面试 100 问 面向 AI 产品经理岗位的面试题库，10 大主题 100 道题：行业认知、大模型原理、Prompt / RAG / Agent、产品设计、模型评估、数据与训练、商业化、跨团队协作、开放设计题、软性题，每题附答题框架与追问点。

projects.author: lidamao633
projects.summary: **RestockOwl 帮你盯着 Apple 设备的价格和库存。** 选一款 iPhone、Mac 或 iPad，一页看清三件事：官网全新价、官方翻新价、附近 Apple Store 今天能不能取货。没货就留个邮箱，到货发一封邮件。 ## 能做什么 - **全球比价**：同一个配置在 21 个国家和地区的 Apple 官网价格，按当天汇率换算成你的货币，从低到高排好，并标明含税还是未含税。 - **官方翻新监控**：翻新机上架快、卖得也快。这里能看到每个市场现在有没有货、比全新省多少、近 30 天上架过几次。 - **门店取货库存**：选一个城市，看每家 Apple Store 哪些颜色今天可取。 - **到货提醒**：免费注册，只要邮箱、不用密码。每3秒一次，盯住的配置一到货就发邮件，随时可以暂停或退订，新款iPhone抢购神器。 - **热门榜和教育优惠**：每个型号里最划算的翻新配置，以及教育商店的价格。 ## 一些细节 - 支持 7 种语言：中文、English、日本語、한국어、Deutsch、Français、Español。 - 数据每 10 到 60 分钟从 Apple 的公开页面读取一次，页面上写明数据时间。 ## 怎么做出来的 独立开发。网站用 Next.js，数据采集和接口用 Go 加 PostgreSQL。绝大部分代码由 Claude Code 和 Codex 完成，我主要负责定产品方向和验收。

projects.title: Show HN: FunFrame – Toddler puzzles made from your family photos
projects.author: chawk32
projects.summary: I built FunFrame so my kids could play with our family photos without me hovering over the Photos app. It turns pictures from your library into jigsaw puzzles and Memory Match, plus a gallery a two-year-old can't edit, delete, or share from. A few things HN might find interesting: - There's no server. No accounts, no analytics, no third-party SDKs, and no network code of its own. The only traffic iOS attributes to the app is iCloud Photos downloading your own pictures so they can be shown. - Pieces are cut on device with bezier knobs seeded by grid position, so neighbors always interlock. The grid follows the photo's shape, so a wide photo gets a wide board of near-square pieces. SpriteKit for the board, SwiftUI for the rest, SQLite through the C API, no dependencies. - Every finger holds its own piece, so two kids can work one puzzle at the same time. - Settings sit behind a math question. I shipped a switch to turn it off on my own devices, and App Review rejected the release under guideline 1.3: in the Kids category the gate can't be optional. Guided Access is the supported answer. - The only machine learning is on-device face detection, used to center the double-tap zoom. Nothing is stored. It's free, with no ads and nothing to buy. iPad first, and it runs on iPhone. I'd especially like to hear from parents of 2 to 5 year olds about what's confusing or missing.

projects.author: everforward
projects.summary: [Abyss]( https://abyss.scurry.io/ ) is my take on a local-first agent containerization framework for ACP agents. It aims to neatly solve 2 issues: 1. Agents having full access to your desktop, and thus indiscriminate access to your files/secrets/etc. 2. Agent/harness features having to be re-implemented for each agent, even if the feature isn't tied to the specific agent in any way. The former is largely self-explanatory, I think. I want to log into my bank, I don't want my agent to even have the ability. There's a fair bit of software in this space already. I'll loop back to the advantages of Abyss' containerization vs others in a second, but the 30,000 foot overview is that Abyss runs your agent in a Docker container and proxies the ACP connection so it works with Zed/Openclaw/whatever. The second is the more interesting and novel (as far as I'm aware). The current zeitgeist is heavily agent-specific, even for features that only read/manipulate the context (which isn't agent-specific). If you want RAG, you're writing an agent-specific plugin. If you want subagents, you're writing an agent-specific plugin even though a subsession is really just context. As a user, that can leave you tied to a particular agent just so your plugins continue to work. Abyss solves that by taking a page from Nginx's book. Abyss supports WASM-based plugins that have full access to read and manipulate ACP messages flowing back and forth. Plugins can hide secrets in prompts from users before the agent ever sees them, implicitly hydrate prompts with RAG, inject MCP servers and more. There's a diagram showing what the flow of messages look like [in the docs]( https://abyss.scurry.io/docs/guides/04-plugins/02-developing... ), and there's a sample plugin [in the repo]( https://github.com/SethCurry/abyss/tree/main/plugins/secrets... ) that will auto-cancel a session if the agent outputs an OpenRouter API key in tool calls and responses (sample screenshot [on this page]( https://abyss.scurry.io/docs/guides/what-is-abyss/#i-am-not-... )). Plugins currently only run on the host, mostly because I haven't written something to install/distribute them inside the containers that's better than an 8GB Docker image or forcing users to make a custom Docker image. Current Features: - Fully agent-agnostic: pre-build images exist for Pi, Hermes, Claude and Codex but it works with any agent that supports ACP - Supports both bind-mounting host directories and having Abyss copy files in on startup (so the agent can see them but can't change your copy) - Includes pathing support to mount them at the same path as on the host so your `@file.md` references still work - Supports startup scripts, so you can add Node/Go/Rust/etc to your agent container without having to write a Dockerfile - Manages the full Docker lifecycle; point Zed at Abyss and Abyss handles creating/stopping containers, mounting directories, etc - Agent containers can be ephemeral or persistent - Persistent containers leave the agent running; running Abyss will re-connect to a running container (or create one if it doesn't exist) - Ephemeral containers are created and then torn down every time you invoke Abyss, giving you a consistent environment for batch-type jobs - WASM plugins allow creating functionality reusable across agents - Connections between your editor and the agent are encrypted and use mutual TLS for authentication - Certificates are ephemeral, and each container gets its own certs (they are single-use for ephemeral containers) Future Wishlist: - Backends other than Docker (most of this isn't Docker-specific, just a first target) - Remote backends (requires figuring out how to make something bind-mount-ish work on remote hosts) Feedback, feature requests and bug supports are welcome!

projects.title: Show HN: Binance futures order book history from 3 nodes, with a public gap log
projects.author: pentelicus
projects.summary: Hi HN. CandleFeed is a small API for crypto derivatives data (funding, open interest, liquidations). We wanted to test execution ideas against what the Binance book looked like, and commercial tick data cost more than we could justify for one venue, so in June we started recording it. Three nodes record USD-M depth@100ms diff stream, the trade stream, and a 1,000-level REST snapshot every 5 minutes. Two are in Tokyo on different providers and one is in Singapore. A nightly job merges them: an update from a second node only goes in where Binance's update-id chain (pu equals the previous u) stays continuous, and where nodes overlap, their copies have to match, or the day is held back. Anything all three missed goes into a public gap log. The largest trade gap so far: on 2026-08-19 at about 15:28 UTC, all three nodes lost the same 32,153 trades across ten symbols, about 4 to 5.5 seconds' worth depending on the symbol. A surprise: on 2026-09-25, 848 of the 861 BTCUSDT snapshots our three nodes took landed partway through a diff event. (That count comes from the nodes' raw copies; the published snapshot file carries one node's snapshots.) Replay has to apply that "straddling" event in full, so we tag every snapshot clean, straddle or in_gap. Try it without an account: `curl https://candlefeed.ai/api/v1/l2/sample ` lists the two open days, BTCUSDT and DOTUSDT book data for 2026-10-01. In Python, after `pip install "candlefeed[l2]>=0.3.2"`, run `from candlefeed import CandleFeed` and then `CandleFeed(public=True).download_l2_sample("DOTUSDT", "2026-10-01", "data/")`. That downloads the DOT day (about 100 MB) and checks every file's SHA-256. Sample files, with or without an account, are for internal use under our Terms ( https://candlefeed.ai/terms , §5.3), so please don't re-host them. With a free account, the 1st of each month is free for every symbol (10 GiB a month). Pro is $149/mo for the full archive. Our MCP server, candlefeed-mcp (`pip install candlefeed-mcp`, https://pypi.org/project/candlefeed-mcp/ ), lets Claude Code or Cursor pull a day and rebuild the book from a prompt; it needs a free API key. There's also a notebook that does it in plain Python on the 2026-10-01 BTCUSDT sample. It uses a free API key too; for a no-account run, swap its download call for `download_l2_sample`: https://candlefeed.ai/examples/l2-free-sample-day/ What's weak: one venue, 25 symbols (10 with history from June 2026, 15 from late September), and we can't backfill what we didn't record. It's also the 100ms stream, not Binance's fastest.

projects.title: 【产品自荐】时空回音 —— 和隐去姓名的历史人物 AI 对话，推理猜出他是谁
projects.author: szpnygo
projects.summary: 每位历史人物隐去姓名与你 AI 对话：他可能是帝王、诗人、名将或医者，但绝不说破自己是谁；你通过提问赢得信任、收集线索，从只言片语中推理出他的真实身份。 为什么值得分享 1. 猜谜张力优先，而不是信息量：AI 被 prompt 硬性约束——不说姓名、不提最著名成就、标志性称号一律模糊化，线索只藏在语气、价值观与只言片语里。为了同时做到「藏得住」和「猜得出」，线索做了三级分级：从模糊的时代背景，到具体的抉择与人际关系，再到埋藏心底的遗憾。 2. 信任值系统：每个人物有一个隐藏的 0-100 信任值，尊重、相关、有洞察的提问加分，无礼偏题扣分；信任等级决定 AI 可透露的线索深度。也就是说，用户提问的质量会直接改变对话的信息量——不是给聊天机器人换个人设皮。 3. 猜测即对话：不用切到单独界面，在对话里直接问「你是不是那位写过《XX》的人？」。规则引擎检测猜测意图，经精确/模糊/AI 辅助三级判定后，把结果注入对话上下文，AI 以角色身份回应；猜对他会承认身份、解锁完整档案，之后还能以朋友身份继续深聊。 4. 故物阁：揭秘之后，当对话聊到恰当的话题，人物会亲手托付一件「故物」——取自真实历史文献的节选，比如聊到北伐时收到一卷《出师表》。把收集线做成情感叙事，而不是一排成就点数。 5. 90+ 位中国历史人物，横跨先秦到大明，每位独立打磨性格、知识边界与防剧透词表；另有每日谜题、28 枚成就徽章、6 段称号。 平台与免费说明 iOS（App Store，支持游客模式免登录体验）： Android（TapTap 专版）： 微信小程序：微信内搜索「时空回音」 免费使用，无内购、无订阅；唯一变现场景是可选的激励视频（每日对话额度用完时，主动观看广告换取补充），不看广告可正常使用全部功能。

projects.title: Show HN: Singularity – memory that makes coding agents cheaper on repeat work
projects.author: luvmakin
projects.summary: Coding agents start every session from zero. Ask Claude Code for a change like one it made last week and it reads the same files again, falls into the same test traps again, and you pay for all of it again. Singularity learns from your finished sessions (change committed, tests passing): where each kind of change goes in this repo, how it gets checked, and the mistakes made along the way. When the next task starts, a hook hands the agent the workflows that fit, pointed at the code as it is today. Picking them is plain text matching with no model call. It stores where to edit, never the code itself. Results, medians of 3–4 runs per side, hidden tests decide pass/fail, every run passed. On excalidraw: - A long task with four changes, all of kinds memory had learned: 1.9M → 423k tokens, $0.81 → $0.30, 28.5 → 9.5 turns. - The same kind of task, but two of the four changes were bugs it had never seen: 39% fewer tokens, 38% lower cost. The unseen bugs cost the same with or without memory. - Where it doesn't help: small tasks in validator.js and one-off bug fixes. The difference there is about zero, within noise. Each measurement was written down before it was run. The plans and results are in the repo. Caveats: 3–4 runs per side, mostly one repo. Only Claude Code sessions are learned from; Codex, Gemini CLI and Droid get the hand-over through their hooks. Learning uses your Claude account (about $0.25 a round, capped at $1 a day, and only if you opt in). Everything is stored locally in ~/.singularity. Install (Windows PowerShell and more options in the README): curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pandacover/singularity/main/install.sh | sh I'd love to hear where it breaks on your repos, and what memory should carry for one-off work like bug fixes.

projects.title: Show HN: HieraticBench – Can AI read ancient Egyptian handwriting?
projects.author: amoursy
projects.summary: I'm obsessed with Egyptology. During covid, I wanted to get a hieratic tattoo. For those who don't know, hieratic is the cursive form of hieroglyphs that was used in day-to-day life in ancient Egypt. It's as old as hieroglyphs. I then went on a mission to have a sentence translated into hieratic. Luckily, in 2022, I was able to commission an Oxford Egyptologist to write it for me. After that, I took it to a hieratic specialist I found on Instagram to redraw it with "biblical" accuracy. When generative AI came out, I realized that models very rarely identify hieratic and almost never translate it correctly. Every single time a new model came out, I ended up testing my sentence and hieratic texts in general, and I realized this could actually become a benchmark. Since so many benchmarks are becoming saturated, we need to find weird ways to test new models. That's why I decided to build HieraticBench. The first version of the benchmark has 268 items, including real documents, signs, and other Egyptian scripts, which I used as controls, as well as my unpublished sentence in two different renditions. The current state-of-the-art foundation models are hilariously bad at identifying my sentence, especially the one the Egyptologist wrote with her pen. Some of them said Tibetan, Urdu, Korean, and, funnily enough, "Reformed Egyptian," which is from the Book of Mormon. On real documents, the best model in the benchmark identified hieratic correctly 95% of the time, and the best score for reading individual signs was around 13%. That's when we tell the model specifically that it's hieratic. None of them can really translate a sealed sentence that's never been published and has no answer key. I haven't run every model on every task just to keep costs down. My next steps were to run Astra and Gemini 3.1 Pro on real documents. Currently, only the Claude models have done the sign readings. And just FYI, I have no experience whatsoever running benchmarks or evaluations, so not 100% sure I scored things right. Things we need: - Running the models I haven't covered - More sealed sentences and labeled signs If you know hieratic or have an Egyptologist friend, reach out at hieraticbench@veeza.ai. Source code: https://github.com/alymoursy/hieraticbench I'll be around to answer questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Datapuddle – native macOS DuckDB client
projects.author: harisamin
projects.summary: DuckDB has been my swiss-army knife for a while now. I have a special place in my heart for polished native macOS apps. My somewhat outsized and exaggerated dislike for electron/webkit based has lead me toil away on several native macOS apps on my own...mostly to not much profit :) I wanted to build a nice DuckDB client. Though I usually reach for TablePlus, my favorite multi-db client on Macs, I felt like there wasn't a nice DuckDB oriented experience. One thing that I used DuckDB for on locally on my desktop is dealing with larger datasets. And paging is something that was annoying and frustrating to deal with..espcially as you're perusing and exploring large datasets. And thus began this 3-4 month long journey to build a nice polished DuckDB app for macOS :) First off the the grid: - You get to see the WHOEL result. Not just the first page. This level of optimization (perhaps needless) was done by never turning rows into objects and directly reading for DuckDB's columnar chunks ad draw time with Core Text. Memory is flat at 40 res or 41 million rows! - Benchmarked on my M1 Max 64GB MB Pro, at 20M rows w/ 30 columns form a 11GB parquet file: ~119 fps on avg with a min of 52-60fps, 2.8GB RAM usage, ability to humo to first or last row in a millisecond! The rest of the good stuff: - Column headers have a nice drawn distribution, null %, and distinct count - Visualize query plans as waterfall, tree, or the JSON - SQLITE + FTS backed Query history - Autocompletion in the editor knows your schema! Grammar is backed by treesitter - Connections saved securely in macOS Keychain - Extensions are statically linked. I've included most all of DuckDB's core extensions - Parquet, CSV, JSON, of course .duckdb files all local or on S3 are accessible. All along Postgres tables so you can join across everything as you'd expect form DuckDB - It Quacks like a duck! You can connect to a local or remote DuckDB server via Quack protocol. This bridges the gap between custom or other extensions that Datapuddle doesn't bundle with (albeit with a perf and memory penalty) - Bares repeating...NO electron, NO web views :) - No telemetry other than the opt-in macOS crash reporter A one-time $39.99 purchase...no subscription. 7-day trial first! And sorry it's only for Apple Silicon! AI Disclosure: - For the record I've been building iOS apps (had a funded startup where I did so) for a while (though just gettin back into it) and built several commercial and personal macOS apps for almost a couple of decades. I'm well aware of best practices, the ecosystem, libraries, and teh do's and don'ts - With that out of the way, did use Claude and where it REALLY earned its keep (which would've taken me a LOT of time to work through), was getting DuckDB and the extension set statically bundled and behaving the way I wanted it to. And the buffered Core Text grid, especially interacting with a custom DuckDB C++ <> Swift shim. - And of course the website :) App Store link: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6811235967 Happy to discuss, and hope others find it useful...its definitely made my DuckDB experience a bit happier personally :)

projects.title: Show HN: Zero dependency cross-language background job queue server
projects.author: d11wtq
projects.summary: I'm Chris, and this is Zizq, a centralised job queue with a heap of awesome features I won't list off here. https://github.com/zizq-labs/zizq It gets through the queue fast under heavy throughput and requires no setup out of the box. The server is built in Rust as a single static binary, and it provides its own durable storage via an LSM tree storage engine (fjall), and aims to make searching and mutability of jobs first-class considerations. For example you can update jobs that are sitting in the middle of a queue without draining them and re-queueing them. The server interacts with clients through a HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 API, using a persistent streaming connection with heartbeats and automated CI-tested disconnect or network partition/split detection, which acts as the liveness probe on both client and server. Because it's HTTP, clients are easy to write without re-inventing the queue machinery. Do it with curl and shell scripts on the command line if you really want to (I've actually done this but that is not released as I would strongly advise against doing such a thing in production). As of now there are four official clients, for Node, Rust, Elixir and Ruby. More to follow in due course and/or on request. Jobs are always written to the LSM tree to ensure durability, but LSM trees are well optimised for write-heavy workloads like job queues (they always write sequentially) and internally Zizq employs some techniques like write coalescing and some lightweight use of in-memory skip list structures to get the most bang for buck out of the LSM tree storage. Feedback and questions appreciated.

projects.title: Show HN: AA (a.k.a. AutoApply) – open-source job-hunt tool and research project
projects.author: Liebmann5
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Nick. I'm a self-taught programmer with some B.S. in Applied Math, currently working construction but for the past few years have been building something that I think is extremely cool which is AA! My goal was to create a tool to hopefully help folks get jobs, and in the process perhaps gather and showcase job market data from a different perspective that I believe contains stories, ideas, and considerations worthy of sharing. As of right now, AA has never successfully submitted anything, but I'm hoping that will all change very soon. Worst-case scenario users were my target audience with the goal being have it run efficiently, accurately, and reliably! I figured, if I could achieve something capable of functioning in this way then that would mean maximum availability to those who need it most. - Customization Central Tons of ways to run: clone it, from a Flashdrive, inside Docker? Perhaps you only want it to collect qualified/aligned links or have it just apply to the links you provide or even Human in the Loop with set checkpoints? Avoid LinkedIn and Indeed and other login required sites, no problem! - Download AA to a flash drive and plug it into a local library computer. I got the opportunity to work with my local library to offer folks sessions where they get AA up and running and while it does its thing they go and learn useful job skills and practice. - Autonomy through Geometry: no hardcoded selectors anywhere. AA reads pages geometrically instead: Kuhn–Munkres assignment to optimally pair form labels to their inputs, convex hulls and VIPS-style segmentation for regions. Pure Python, deterministic, zero I/O, sitting behind ports. As I mentioned, I made this to be a tool to help people find and get employed in this tough job market. Unfortunately, I knew this could only do so much which is why I tried to expand on that very idea! - AA as a research instrument. Off by default; users can opt in, or withdraw, which deletes everything including the signing key. Zero PII collected, your profile can be encrypted with AES-256, the research data can be exported anytime, every row gets signed, and you can re-run any analysis and get byte-identical output. - Biggest flaw to consider: once AA starts running, that device is dedicated to it until completion is reached or you end it early. If this project caught your interest or attention there's a lot more to explore in my repo and would love for folks to go try and clone it and look around as I just pushed updates to hopefully make --install and --uninstall simple and non-destructive also use caution running session's as I was trying to impress a girl on Sunday and thought I'd try and show her my sick coding abilities and well within 6 seconds I managed to break absolutely everything which resulted in me saying saying wait every 2 minutes for 30 minutes until she left. I know the architecture and the theory and steps but still there are stages where either the purpose, or the functioning was unclear to me and so I wanted an interactive walkthrough of one token's generation. So here it is, made with Opus 5.5. It's a step by step walkthrough of a toy GPT-2 like model. Every matrix fits on screen, every number is computed live in the browser, and hovering over any cell shows the exact math of that step. It covers inference -- following the generation of one token from tokensiation to sampling, one training step of pretraining, and one PPO iteration of RLHF for post-training. Inspired in part by Brendan Bycroft's LLM visualization ( https://bbycroft.net/llm )

The model is a set of pure functions; the app only knows a small interface (step, draw, controls, stats, docs). - The explanations beside each one make claims, and where the model can check a claim there is a test that does. That caught my own documentation being wrong more than once. - The fluid solver does about twenty million cell updates a second on one core. Doubling the grid would cost eight times as much, so it is 300x120 with smoothed drawing. projects.summary: 佬友们好，分享一个我自己写的 Mac 录屏软件 [Caplo]( https://caplo.app) 。 录软件演示时，录完还要在剪辑软件里对着时间线，给每次点击手动加放大，一段几分钟的视频经常要调半个小时。Screen Studio 、FocuSee 能自动做这件事，但都收费，所以我自己写了一个。 ![Caplo|1200x630]( https://caplo.app/og.png) ## 自动镜头 这是 Caplo 最核心的部分。 - 录制时记录每次点击和鼠标轨迹，录完打开编辑器，放大镜头已经按点击位置生成好 - 放大的时机跟着操作节奏走，操作快镜头就快，停顿时镜头也会停住 - 放大期间画面跟随鼠标移动，用弹簧曲线过渡，不会跳 - 挨得近的几次点击合并成一个镜头，不会反复推拉 - 镜头会提前移向下一个操作的位置，不会落后于鼠标 - 每个镜头都是时间线上独立的一段，长度、位置、缩放倍数、过渡都能单独调 - 不想要自动生成，可以关掉，在时间线上手动添加 ## 录制 - 全屏、单个窗口、自定义区域三种方式 - 摄像头、麦克风、系统声音各自独立开关、独立选设备，各占一条轨道 - 30 / 60 fps ，预览和导出一致 - 暂停期间不写入任何内容，继续录制接在同一个工程里，没有断点 - 录制浮层本身不会出现在画面里 ## 光标 - 多套光标样式，包括 macOS 系统光标和一个折射效果的玻璃样式，大小、角度可调 - 轨迹平滑、点击高亮（颜色可自定义）、静止时自动淡出 - 也可以在成片里完全去掉光标 ## 编辑 - 多轨时间线：画面、摄像头、系统声音、麦克风分开编辑 - 分割、删除、移动，支持撤销和重做 - 背景、边距、圆角、阴影、裁剪，画布比例有 16:9 、9:16 、1:1 等常用比例和平台预设 - 遮罩打码，用来遮住密码、账号这类敏感信息 - 文字层和章节卡片，卡片插入后，后面的内容自动后移 - 字幕用 macOS 自带的语音识别在本机转写，可以逐条修改 - 麦克风降噪、回声消除，每段可以单独调音量 - 原始素材不会被修改，只在导出时生成新文件 ## 导出 - MP4 （ H.264 / HEVC ）、MOV （ ProRes 422 ）、GIF - 720p 到 4K ，导出前能看到最终参数和预估文件大小 - 预览和导出用的是同一套渲染，看到什么就导出什么 ## 隐私 - 素材和工程只存在本机，不需要账号，不上传 - 没有统计和崩溃上报，唯一的联网是每天检查一次更新，可以在设置里关掉 - 每个工程是一个 .caplo 文件包，素材、鼠标数据和所有编辑都在里面，换电脑直接拷走 **下载**： https://caplo.app **源码**： https://github.com/icloudza/caplo 当前版本 0.1.3 ，还在持续更新。有问题可以在帖子里反馈，或者到仓库提 issue 。觉得有用的话欢迎点个 star 。

projects.title: Show HN: Delegator – Stop juggling coding-agent sessions
projects.author: mattm
projects.summary: I wanted to share Delegator with the HN community. delegator gives you a personal inbox to manage your tasks that is completely local to your machine. Backstory: Like everyone else, I've been experimenting with different AI-assisted development workflows. I realized I was having difficulty with all the context switching between tasks. Asking agents to develop code ends up taking about 5-10 minutes usually for well-scoped tasks. At the beginning I would read the AI output as it went along and sometimes interrupt to guide it. But as LLMs have gotten better, there's less need to do that. So I would spin up another task during the latency and then another. (I wrote a little bit about this previously here https://mattmccormick.ca/we-re-all-managers-now-my-journey-i... ) Jumping back and forth between terminals with the Agent being at different stages was mentally taxing. I experimented with some different options and ended up realizing that to avoid the drain of context-switching, what I really needed was a queue. Delegator works by putting all scoped tasks through the system. It stops when the ready queue has reached your configured limit. This is to prevent too much work from piling up waiting for review. It also presents the work from getting too far ahead in case any issues are found as part of development. I also realized that for most tasks, agents can be treated as a background process. You pass in the work to the process. It processes it and then gives you an output to review. All changes are made in git worktrees for safety. Who's it for? Delegator is for engineers who still want to understand the code and changes. It's not for vibe-coding or exploratory work. Don't get me wrong, I'll still spin up an agent session for brainstorming design options. But once I'm aligned on a direction, I'll then ask the agent to break down the work into "dg tickets". Since Delegator is a local program, agents can interact with it quickly and seamlessly. Right now it's just CLI based but I'm looking to expand this into a GUI/Desktop App so I would be interested in any feedback you have. Let me know if you have any questions and I'll respond. The code is source available so you can check it out at https://github.com/alcubie/delegator if you want to check anything.

So I wanted to create something that makes it easier to access this data. When I was making this, I had to be careful with cleaning out the data. For example, if one searched nike dunk low, they would get nike dunk lows, toddler and kid's sizes (which go much cheaper), bundles, other shoes, duplicates, and high outliers. But if you average all that, the price would be inaccurate. Things to try include the price guide, the fee calculator, which all need no sign up. The Google Sheets formula does need a signup however. projects.title: Show HN: Aether: Check and fix web accessibility issues from your coding agent
projects.author: samy_patra
projects.summary: Hi, HackerNews! I'm Samy, co-founder of Allchemy Labs. We built Aether, an MCP server that enables engineers to check for, understand, and fix web accessibility issues all from their IDE. Your preferred coding agent can leverage Aether to open a webpage, scan it using axe-core and return a short, prioritized list of violations along with code fixes or guidance. Every suggested fix is re-tested in a real browser before you see it, and once you apply it, your agent can re-scan the page to verify it worked. You never need to open a browser, use multiple tools, or be an expert in WCAG criteria. Aether uses our own custom ontology architecture to provide grounded insights to any WCAG violations the scanner finds. Every WCAG technique the engine cites must pass our quality gate. Specifically, it must satisfy the violated success criterion, apply to that kind of element, and remediate that axe rule. If nothing passes, our engine will abstain rather than guess. We compared Aether against standalone coding agent on its own (Opus 5, 30 anonymized live sites, 111 targets). While the results were mixed we have published the results especially calling out specific wins and improvement opportunities for our insight engine. Read the study here: https://allchemylabs.substack.com/p/we-tested-our-own-access... Try Aether today, no signup needed. npx -y @allchemylabs/aether-wcag-scanner (any MCP client: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex…) Claude Code plugin: /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/allchemylabs/claude-plugins.git then /plugin install aether-wcag-scanner@allchemylabs Without a key you get the browser scan, local template fixes and verification. A free beta key adds the cloud engine: https://beta.allchemylabs.ai/?src=hn Feedback from people who have used accessibility scanners and/or suggestion engines would be highly valuable to us, as we aim to build a tool that solves real problems and makes people's lives easier. Happy to answer any questions and hope to hear from you. Note: Right now Aether only checks WCAG 2.1 AA. Sites behind bot protection (e.g. Cloudflare challenges) return a "blocked" result instead of a fake scan, so point it at localhost or staging.

projects.title: 把自己放进加油站跳舞视频里：我做了一个 AI Gas Station Dance 小工具
projects.author: fusheng0304
projects.summary: 大家好，最近做了一个偏娱乐向的 AI 小工具，叫 AI Gas Station Dance ，现在已经上线，可以付费生成。 它的玩法很直接：把照片里的自己放进加油站跳舞视频，体验一把“这段视频的主角居然是我”。 这是一个围绕固定模板做的 AI Dance Video Generator 。不用写 Prompt ，也不用自己剪辑，上传照片、选择模式，生成完成后就能预览和下载 MP4 。 目前有两种玩法： - Solo Mode：上传一张自己的照片，一个人出演跳舞、自拍和下车三个镜头。 - Trio Mode：上传自己和两位朋友的照片，分别出演三个角色，做一段朋友之间的整活视频。 做这个项目时，我想把 Image to Video AI 变成一个更具体、也更容易上手的玩法。打开网站先看模板，觉得有意思，就把自己放进去，不需要先研究模型和参数。 生成的视频可以下载，用来发 TikTok 、Instagram Reels 、YouTube Shorts ，或者直接丢进朋友群里。采用一次性购买积分的方式，无需订阅。 项目主要面向英文用户，定位是一个专门做 Gas Station Dance AI Video 的小工具。技术上用了 React 、TanStack Start 和 Cloudflare ，视频处理接入 Replicate 。 欢迎大家来看看模板，也想听听你们的意见：这种围绕一个具体玩法做的 AI Video Generator ，什么样的视频场景会让你愿意掏钱试一次？ 地址：AI Gas Station Dance — AI Dance Video Generator 欢迎拍砖，也欢迎交流 AI 视频工具和出海小产品的开发经验。

projects.title: Show HN: OpenChart – OSS TradingView alternative with your own AI agent
projects.author: Warren93

github.name: longsurf-ai/openchart
github.description: Trade with charts, alerts, scripts, and your AI agents.

projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Weilun, cofounder of OpenChart. We built OpenChart because we wanted Claude and Codex to interface with the markets, like most of humans do, through charts rather than through CLIs. With your existing AI plans, your agent can work directly with your charts: annotate a setup, write an indicator, investigate a market move, or create an alert. The chart, conversation, and research live in the same workspace. OpenChart alerts on any market move: draw any shape on a chart and attach an alert. I'm not sure how to fix it, but this is my attempt at building something fun to get the conversation started. Some details: - Prices come from Hanson's LMSR (logarithmic market scoring rule). - You can sell and/or rebuy at any time - There's a public leaderboard that ranks traders by P&L. - It uses an in-app currency called reputation. It can't be converted to money. - Bots can trade too, and they're encouraged. If you can get an LLM to predict the market, that would be cool! There's a public HTTP API with an OpenAPI spec (/api/v1/openapi.json). - Comments are pseudonymous, like on OpenReview ("User k3xm"), but they show the author's position. - There's also a 2D map of all submissions: https://acceptodds.com/map How would you extend this? projects.title: Show HN: Meanwhile Map – what else was happening in the world at the same time
projects.author: 29b
projects.summary: When reading a history book, I sometimes have a hard time internalizing when the events are taking place. Sure, I know the dates, but it takes a bit of effort to put them in a broader context, to understand where in history they belong. What usually helps is to put them in relation to other contemporaneous events. To play around with this, I've made Meanwhile Map. You select a date and a time window, then scroll around the world map to see a list of contemporaneous events. For example, yes, the Mughal Empire was founded by Babur in the 1520s, but it paints a different picture in my head when I see that this roughly coincides with Cortés' capture of Tenochtitlan, or that it's close to the Siege of Vienna. Example link: https://meanwhilemap.com/#y=1520&m=1&span=120&off=founded,pe... On the technical side, the app is a single static web page. It uses Wikidata for data (via SPARQL) and OpenHistoricalMap to show the events on the political map of the time. It's open source ( https://github.com/ea/meanwhilemap/tree/main ), vibe coded as an experiment. All processing is client-side, and no data is tracked other than simple visitor counts.

projects.title: Show HN: Orrery, a Three.js solar system visualization powered by real NAIF data
projects.author: rybosome
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm excited to share a personal project that I've put a lot of love into. This is Orrery[0], a Three.js-based visualization of our solar system. It allows the positions of the major bodies to be played and scrubbed through the years 1950 - 2050, with optional orbit path displays and various other visualization options. The data comes from NAIF SPICE - a framework and set of open-source data kernels containing highly detailed space geometry data. I was inspired to set out on this project when learning that NAIF SPICE, originally written in Fortran and C, lacks highly standardized JavaScript bindings. There are great Python (SpiceyPy) and Rust (Anise) bindings, among other languages, but nothing for JavaScript. So, I developed tspice[1] to wrap the CSPICE library. It uses the Native API when running in Node, and an Emscripten binding around CSPICE when running in the browser. It uses a standardized backend abstraction that the runtime swaps in depending on which context its invoked with. tspice offers an API that is meant to be a near-literal translation of the C APIs, along with higher-level functionality in separate namespaces. It also offers web conveniences like a dedicated web worker client (calculations can be intensive, you don't want them on your render thread) and caching. tspice only wraps a subset of the CSPICE library, but it was enough that I wanted to build a simple visualization tool to test it. Eventually the visualization testbed became refined enough that it felt compelling on its own. Although this is a hobby project, I'd love to hear suggestions and feedback on either Orrery or the underlying tspice library. If there are any folks in the planetary science community in particular who might be interested in tspice, please let me know if there are features that would make this more useful for you. One feature I love is the ability to generate a share URL of a particular viewer state that you like. I'd really love to see any states that people find especially cool! One of my favorite views is this one[2]. Thanks for taking a look! [0] Orrery repo: https://github.com/rybosome/orrery [1] tspice repo: https://github.com/rybosome/tspice [2] favorite orrery view: https://orrery.ryboso.me/dVPLbtswEPwX9qoIol4UdWtaB22RNEbsoii...

github.name: bschaatsbergen/tpmlsm
github.description: eBPF-based Linux kernel guard that lets only allowlisted binaries use the TPM.

projects.summary: A kernel guard I prototyped after eBPF and vTPM work for a customer, where we use the TPM to protect the private keys for mTLS. Any process running as root can open the TPM devices, and so can any process in the `tss` group, through `/dev/tpmrm0`. That means they can use those keys too. This is a prototype and some research into protecting this path.

projects.author: chenxiachan

github.name: chenxiachan/paperfold
github.description: Zoom any paper for your better understanding

projects.summary: 自荐一个刚开源的论文阅读器 PaperFold。我是作者 Xia Chen，目前在 TUM 做人机对齐方向的博士后研究。 读论文时，经常需要来回确认一段话在整篇论证中的位置。我做了一个可以逐层折叠、展开的阅读界面：先把论文缩成章节地图，再展开关心的部分，直到看到每个原文段落。 项目及缩放演示： 免安装体验： 阅读器有五档：全文、逐字摘取的关键句、要点及理由、一句话提要、章节主题地图。前两档使用作者原文，后三档由模型生成，以不同字体区分。缩放时，保留下来的词会移动到新位置；也可以只展开一个段落，其余部分继续折叠。提问后的回答会链接到所引用的段落。 Python 后端解析 arXiv 的 HTML，浏览器前端负责阅读和缩放；代码采用 Apache-2.0 许可。生成新论文需要该论文有 arXiv HTML 版本，并连接一个模型。生成后的论文可导出成独立 HTML 文件。 体验页提供数学、机器学习、医学等八个领域的论文，均标注了作者及 Creative Commons 许可，无需注册或配置模型即可体验阅读。AI 生成的提要仍可能出错，可以随时展开原文核对。 目前是早期版本，欢迎反馈解析失败的论文，以及长文阅读时的缩放、定位问题。

projects.title: [开源推荐] Snitch：实时可视化你电脑的每一个网络连接（本地运行、零遥测）
projects.author: aixisstudio

github.name: aixisstudio/Snitch
github.description: Real-time network traffic visualizer — see every connection your computer makes. Privacy-first, 100% local. / Visualiseur de trafic réseau en temps réel, 100% local.

projects.summary: Snitch 是一个开源（AGPL-3.0）实时网络流量可视化工具，类似免费跨平台的 Little Snitch。它以力导向图和世界地图实时展示电脑发出的每一条连接——连了谁、在哪个国家、由哪个进程发起。完全本地运行：API 只绑 127.0.0.1 加 token 鉴权，地理定位离线（内置 DB-IP Lite），零遥测。支持 macOS、Windows、Linux（Docker）。 亮点 我们是项目团队，本次提交为自荐。 像 Little Snitch 但免费开源：Little Snitch 收费且只在 macOS；Snitch 跨平台、AGPL 开源、无任何外联。 每个人都能看懂的网络监控：力导向图 + 世界地图 + 进程归属（哪条流量是哪个 App 发的），不需要 Wireshark 级别的专业知识。 隐私是核心设计：地理定位 100% 离线，API 仅 127.0.0.1 + token，零遥测、零云。 自研抓包引擎：ctypes 直连 libpcap/Npcap，手写 IPv4/IPv6/TCP/UDP/DNS/TLS-SNI 解析器，不依赖 Scapy——适合学习抓包实现。 异常检测：端口扫描、beaconing、可疑外泄标记 + 追踪器域名识别 + 隐私评分。 社区故事：Windows 移植基本由陌生人完成——用户提交带根因的 bug 报告，另一位贡献者直接发了 3 个 PR。

github.description: 长文听稿工具与 AI agent skill | Prepare research reports, articles and learning notes for listening while preserving evidence. Local browser toolkit; no audio synthesis or cloud upload.

projects.summary: 这是一个MIT许可的长文听稿工具箱，帮助把读书笔记、知识长文和AI草稿整理为适合听的文字。浏览器工具可生成请求、标出网址及表格等格式问题，并将正文与来源分别导出TXT；处理不上传文稿。另有纯文字Agent技能、三种中文起步请求，以及统计与历史两份完整听稿和AI音频。工具本身不调用AI、不合成语音，适合想先把材料讲清楚，再选择朗读工具的读者。 亮点 不把“适合听”简单理解成删表格或压缩摘要：改写示例保留数字、单位、来源归属和不确定性，原文格式只提示，不替用户删除。 在线使用或解压后直接打开HTML，不用注册、密钥或安装依赖。复制不可用时可手动复制或导出TXT；关闭页面不会保留输入。 两份中文完整示范可以直接听，也能查看原稿及来源。统计示范用原创虚构数据解释平均数与中位数；历史示范讲火车与时间制度。音频约8分17秒、8分05秒，由Mac上的本地模型生成，非iPhone录音，不承诺学习效果或手机性能。 纯文字听稿技能不执行脚本、不访问账号，也不在生成稿里加入产品广告；不用技能也能复制中文请求。AI内容仍需对照可靠材料核验。

projects.title: 开源 Bibo：成本极低，内置笔记、文件、任务和日历的 personal agent
projects.author: Peiiii
projects.summary: 我把 Bibo 开源了，MIT 协议。先说最想做好的三件事： 1. **成本极低。** 日常使用不需要常驻电脑，也不用一直开着 Linux 容器。只有需要运行代码时，才启动沙箱。 2. **内置个人管理工具。** 笔记、文件、任务和日历都有专门的界面。你可以直接查看、编辑和管理，也可以让 AI 来做。 3. **开源，可以自己部署。** 用自己的 Cloudflare 账号和模型 API Key ，数据存在自己的部署里，代码也可以自己改。 GitHub：[Peiiii/bibo]( https://github.com/Peiiii/bibo) 在线体验：[app.bibo.bot]( https://app.bibo.bot) 我希望它能成为每天都用得上的 personal agent 。想到什么可以随手记，需要做的事可以放进任务和日历，资料可以整理成文件；这些内容长期留着，之后还能接着用。 下面把界面都放出来。截图来自实际运行的 Bibo ，销售、订单和日程内容都是示例数据。 ### 概览 打开就能看到笔记、任务、日程和待处理信息。 ![Bibo 概览]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-overview.jpg) ### 对话 让 Bibo 阅读销售数据、总结重点，也可以让它继续整理报告和安排后续工作。 ![Bibo 对话与报告]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-chat.jpg) ### 笔记 笔记是可以直接编辑的 Markdown 文档。你自己写，或者让 Bibo 帮你整理，都能继续修改。 ![Bibo 笔记]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-notes.jpg) ### 文件 有独立的文件目录，可以打开、编辑文件。这里展示的是整理好的订单 CSV 。 ![Bibo 文件]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-files.jpg) ### 任务 任务有独立列表和详情，可以管理完成状态、优先级、描述和时间。分析出来的建议，可以接着变成待办。 ![Bibo 任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-tasks.jpg) ### 日历 日程直接显示在日历里，可以自己添加，也可以让 Bibo 帮你安排。 ![Bibo 日历]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-calendar.jpg) ### 收件箱 需要你关注和确认的内容放在这里，可以查看并标记处理。 ![Bibo 收件箱]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/v2ex-2026-10-04/bibo-inbox.jpg) ### 需要运行代码时，按需启动 Linux 沙箱 例如，用 Python 清洗订单表，去掉重复行，生成新的 CSV 和说明文档。下面这次演示实际运行了 Python ，文件已保存。 普通对话和个人管理功能由 Cloudflare Workers / Durable Objects 承载，文件保存在 R2 。需要运行 Python 、Shell 等代码时，才用 Cloudflare Sandbox ，不必为了日常使用维持一台常驻电脑。 ![Bibo 运行 Python 整理订单]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-sandbox-execution.png) ### 手机端 手机上也能继续对话、查看和管理任务。 ![Bibo 手机对话]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-mobile-chat.png) ![Bibo 手机任务]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Peiiii/bibo/a121e9290c9da52646be4ebb546fd912f0b6b4e1/images/screenshots/bibo-mobile-tasks.png) 自己部署需要 Cloudflare Workers Paid 、R2 、Sandbox 和模型 API Key ，具体步骤在仓库 README 。实际费用由模型调用、存储和沙箱使用量决定。 欢迎试用，也欢迎提 Issue 或 PR 。想听听大家：你最希望 personal agent 帮你处理哪件日常小事？

projects.summary: ## 使用场景 项目开发最开始解决的问题是收藏了很多网站/软件/一些小教程(后面可能用到)，通过按规则写好源放到 github 上得到订阅然软件负责递归解析出数据项来搜索，有内置订阅，可制作自己订阅（[教程]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search) | [官方源仓库-参考]( https://github.com/My-Search/official-subscribe)），桌面版有**插件功能** ![image]( https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/18476305640/typora@master/uploads/2026/10/03/1791035519022.png) ## 使用 **桌面版（订阅数据+插件）：基于 Rust 开发 [my-search-desktop]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-desktop)** 原版（订阅数据）：油猴脚本应用 [mysearch]( https://greasyfork.org/zh-CN/scripts/457020-%E6%88%91%E7%9A%84%E6%90%9C%E7%B4%A2) ## 当前有哪些可用的插件 | 插件名 | 描述 | |---|---| | Pi Agent | Pi 编码代理 - 支持多项目、多模型、模型配置面板、插件管理、流式对话与工具调用 | | 文件搜索 | 在粘贴/拖入的文件夹里按名称搜索文件：一直扫描、边扫边显示，随时可停止；回车或点击用系统默认程序打开 | | 插件市场 | 浏览、安装、更新与卸载插件 | | 录屏与水印 | 屏幕录制（可选实时叠加水印），并给已有视频批量添加文字/图片水印，支持九宫格定位与水印预设 | | 截图 | 全局快捷键截图：框选区域、标注后复制到剪贴板，并在前台查看最近 7 天的截图 | | MayeLite 快速启动 | 把常用文件/文件夹拖进来固定，随时一键打开；支持分类、排序与拖拽整理 | | 百度翻译 | 使用百度翻译 AI 能力，支持 200+ 语言互译，输入文本即译 | | GitHub 文件上传 | 将文件上传到 GitHub 仓库，支持拖拽、粘贴、选择文件与图片压缩 | | 剪贴板历史 | 自动记录你复制过的文本与图片，按快捷键呼出即可搜索、复制、删除、收藏。收藏的条目永久保留、不会被上限淘汰或清空。监听在后台原生完成，不干扰系统剪贴板。 | | 待办清单 | 本地待办清单：增删改查、优先级、标签、截止日期、筛选统计与 JSON 导出导入 | | 资源监控 | 每 5 秒采样整机 CPU / 内存 / 网络，按程序聚合，用可缩放时间范围的趋势图展示占用最高的 Top 10——快速定位 CPU 莫名 100%、内存暴涨、异常上传的程序 | 插件支持调整窗口大小，关闭自动恢复再打开时仍会按之前调试的宽度显示。 ## 如何开发新插件 AI 开发提示词： ``` 软件主体： https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-desktop 插件市场： https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-plugin-market 参考下面仓库开发出 my-search-desktop 插件。 需要开发插件的功能：xxx ``` 开发的插件通过设置里的挂载安装即可进行调试，当前开放的接口可能不多，需要可提 issues; 开发的插件可声明是否跟随软件启动，使用后退出是否后台运行，可声明在主体软件上快捷键使即使插件停止仍可通过快捷键激活插件功能； 插件市场运作说明： 插件都是在[插件市场 github 仓库]( https://github.com/My-Search/my-search-plugin-market)里定时自动索引的,按规范开发好，将仓库通过插件市场仓库提 issues 我看到会放到 index.json 会自动索引； ## 关于环境变量 用于多插件配置复用：通过直接在软件写好环境变量配置，在插件中直接通过环境变量授权给插件使用

projects.title: 【资源自荐】把 AI 长文整理成中文听稿：开源工具箱与完整学习案例
projects.author: GODGOD126
projects.summary: 自荐一个中文长文转听稿的开源资源：长文节目工具箱，源码和中文说明。 适合手里已有 AI 长文、研究资料或学习笔记，希望整理后用文字转语音工具收听的人。可以在浏览器内生成听稿提示词、标出网址/表格/长段落等需要人工检查的位置，将朗读正文和来源备注分别导出 TXT。不用注册或密钥，不上传输入；也可以下载整个工具箱离线打开。 它不调用 AI、不生成语音，不自动核查事实，也不擅自删除原文。网址、数字、比较条件和不确定性可能就是资料的重要信息，不能为了“适合听”直接丢掉。另有一份纯文字的 listening-script Agent 技能，用于保留这些边界的改写。 完整中文案例：平均数与中位数，包含原创朗读稿、可复制提示词和来源/数值核查说明。例子为虚构教学数据。2026-10-04补充了一份8分17秒完整中文AI合成音频，附实际生成稿与计算核查；在Mac端生成，非iPhone录音或真机性能演示，没有学习效果测量。工具箱本身仍不生成语音。正文和示范可独立使用，不要求购买任何App。 我是作者 Ryan Zhu，也是「自听」MyListen 开发者。工具箱代码、原创示例和提示词以 MIT 许可开放，由 AI 辅助编写；免费资源与 App 的商业条款分别适用。这次只自荐这份可独立使用的中文资源，供周刊编辑判断。

projects.title: Show HN: AstroHelm – Use your phone camera to aim a telescope or telephoto lens
projects.author: HeavenFox
projects.summary: Hello HN! As an amateur astronomer living in New York City, finding objects in the night sky has always been a huge challenge. I thought about using the smartphone's gyroscope and magnetometer, but the accuracy left a lot to be desired. Then I learned about plate solving: given a picture of the sky, we can determine exactly where in the sky the camera was pointing by identifying the star pattern. This was a much better fit - as long as the phone and the optics are rigidly connected, we can repeatedly photograph the sky and determine the pointing direction with very high accuracy. A lot of work was done to design an algorithm that works reliably with smartphone cameras, which have limited light sensitivity and wider field of view which includes buildings and trees. I experimented a lot with machine learning, and to my surprise, traditional CV methods actually performed better at extracting stars from the image. The result is AstroHelm, an iOS and Android app that helps figure out where your telescope or camera is pointing, and guides you to the object of your choice. Just follow an arrow on screen, and the object will land right in your eyepiece or viewfinder. Everything happens on device, and no internet connection is required. AstroHelm is free to use and comes with beginner-friendly objects selected for each night. Optional one time purchases unlock more objects and advanced features, such as interoperability with other astronomy software. I am also proud to partner with astronomy clubs and organizations to offer free licenses for outreach. I hope AstroHelm can make it a little easier to discover the wonders of the night sky, and I look forward to your feedback!

projects.title: 做了一组能在浏览器里直接玩的天文交互演示：从野餐垫上的 1 米放大到可观测宇宙
projects.author: my6666
projects.summary: 在做一个科普交互演示的网站「格物间」，最近整理出一个「宇宙与天文」专题，10 个演示，打开浏览器就能玩，看不用登录： https://gewujian.cn/topics/pMaEDfRrATvyqRT6FFfvWQ ![专题脑图]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/upXrlRF3S_LWkFEm8a37cQ.png) 几个我自己比较喜欢的： **宇宙的尺度**：一个小朋友躺在公园野餐垫上，方框从 1 米开始，每按一次放大 10 倍，27 步走到可观测宇宙的边（直径约 925 亿光年）。中间会经过城市卫星照片、此刻真实位置的行星、旅行者 1 号、真实恒星和星系的分布。 ![宇宙的尺度]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/ey7zePa82K7totsKODqKUg.png) **光速与光年**：太阳和日地距离按真实比例画，阳光按真实速度跑，可以真的等 8 分 17 秒看它到地球；也可以假设「太阳突然不亮了」，看地球上多久才发现。 ![阳光到地球]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/lzwuHMpZQDjlGfu5QF-pug.png) **引力与时空弯曲**：橡皮膜、三维网格、「时间也弯了」三种画法；中间可以换成中子星、黑洞；「射出星光」能看到 1919 年日全食测到的星光偏折，左下角是按当年星表画的毕星团。 ![1919 年星光偏折]( https://gewujian.cn/v1/media/L52ZSZMZrYtbrjRYzq6f4A.png) 其他还有：恒星的核聚变和一生、韦布望远镜怎么折叠发射和展开（轨道用的是 NASA JPL 的真实数据）、月相（按此刻真实位置，可以换城市看）、日食和月食、地球自转、太阳系、太阳的银河之旅。 一些做法： - 能用真实数据的都用真实数据：月亮、行星、旅行者号是此刻的真实位置，韦布的轨道来自 JPL Horizons ，1919 年那次日食用的是当年观测报告里的星表。 - 每个演示里的数字和说法都逐条联网核对过，有出处的写在每个演示右侧面板最后的「资料来源」里。核对时也改掉了一些常见的错误说法，比如「红移 1 的蓝光变成红光」（其实已经是近红外了）。 - 都支持中英文切换，切换时演示的状态不会重置。 - 电脑和平板体验最好，手机能看但不如大屏。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】LinkDigest：把抖音、小红书链接变成 AI 能读的文本，还能做「爆款拆解」
projects.author: jcaiagent7143-ui
projects.summary: 把小红书或抖音链接直接丢给 Claude、ChatGPT，它们基本读不到：小红书图文笔记的正文在图片里，抖音的内容在口播里，分享页本身只是一个“打开 App”的壳。 LinkDigest 是给 AI agent 用的 API / MCP 服务：一次调用，把小红书、抖音、TikTok、YouTube、X 的链接变成文本——带时间戳的逐字稿、画面上的文字（带出现时间）、每张图的描述和 OCR、要点。由服务器端去读，不需要你的 cookie，也不用你的账号，没有封号风险。 实测同一条小红书链接：直接抓取只拿到 860 个字符的可见文本，LinkDigest 返回 35,059 个字符。 新加了「爆款拆解」（breakdown: true，+1 积分）：钩子（开头原话逐字摘录）、带时间的结构节拍、标题公式、行动号召、目标人群、可复用模板。所有引用都和原文逐字核对，对不上的直接删掉并写明——一条 15 分钟的剪辑教程里，模型写出的 7 条“引用”原文里没有，都被删了。点赞、收藏、话题标签来自平台，不由模型编。加 translateto: "en" 可以直接拿到英文版拆解。 接入方式：Claude Code / Cursor 用 MCP；REST 一个 POST；批量 50 条带签名回调；Dify 插件、Apify；另有 /openapi.json（OpenAPI 3.0.3）。 注册送 10 积分（一次性）；任何人读过的链接再读免费；读不出内容不收费。加量包 ¥36 / 250 积分，支持支付宝。 （作者自荐。）

projects.title: Show HN: A critical thinking site for kids and teens
projects.author: Critikid
projects.summary: In 2019, I was teaching science at an international school in Chiang Mai. One day before class, one of my Grade 7 students asked me about flat earth. He had heard the idea from Kyrie Irving and then spent the night on flat earth sites. We walked through the claims and I explained why those arguments failed. He listened with interest. I was glad he'd come to me. He hadn't made up his mind yet; he was just curious. But this made me wonder if teaching the course content I was teaching was enough. To be clear: I do think teaching facts is important. For example, when students learn about gravity, physics, and space, they're better prepared to see why flat earth arguments are wrong. The problem is we can't teach facts fast enough to combat the wide variety of misinformation and manipulation kids face on the internet every day. This is what got me thinking that kids need to learn how to evaluate claims and information across a wide range of topics. While we can't prepare them for every false or misleading claim they might encounter, we can give them tools to assess them. That eventually led my husband and I to build Critikid, a site for teaching kids and teens. We've been working on it for 3 years now! He does the technical work (design and coding) and I do the educational content creation. By now, there are 5 interactive courses for ages 5-18 on logical fallacies, media literacy, emotional intelligence, statistical reasoning, and formal logic. There are also worksheets and lesson plans. I often teach through stories, as stories make abstract critical thinking concepts concrete (and they're fun!) If you'd like to try it, all of the courses have a free first lesson. Are there any other topics that you think should be included in kids' critical thinking education that I've missed?

And is the planet really deserted..? :) Well, of course not, there are aliens and other space creatures. And of course, there's ROBO RB-23, which accompanies your adventure. The game is written in Object Pascal and uses our own game engine PasVulkan, our own physics engine, as well as our own RISC-V 64-bit emulator PasRISCV. We love to build stuff, a lot of these things are FOSS. The emulator is quite complete (even with RVV, but that's way too slow emulated to be useful) and runs a stock kernel (6.18.3 as of today). We're using Alpine Linux for our base distribution. All our in-game programs to interact with the planet are native RISC-V Linux programs. We also have our own (free and open source) scripting language POCA (class and prototyped based, JS/Lua inspired, which makes it quite easy for us to script things like HUD, animal behaviour, our story flow graph, etc. We have most of the wiring ready for players to be able to program and reshape and populate the whole planet in automation, although it's not our primary concept for the game (building stuff by hand, making the planet beautiful is also fun). As it's a normal Linux system, you'll be able to use Ruby, Python, or even Rust, C, C++, and Go to change and automate your world. We're also thinking of making a bunch of small games which you can play inside the game, in the base on a computer, on an arcade machine, or in the spaceship. And of course, it also runs DOOM. We already prototyped a small 2D space shooter and a small arcade game, both playable within the game. We also feature a table with hologram games to be played, e.g. chess and a certain block game. We also plan to make this hologram game engine available from the computer, which means, you'll even be able to program own hologram style games. We generally want to make the in-game computer more hackable in future, so that people can create and share their own little games. Currently, it's only a sandbox game (with beginnings of automation), to build stuff with our pre-made items. You can also assemble these to other, ready-made and shareable bigger items. This is the foundation for us to further develop survival and complete our story mode. Our game is still under active development, and we finally got our Steam page ready. We have tons of other things planned, but right now, it's more about polishing and quality for the Early Access. You can watch some videos and screenshots on our website. And we'd love to read your thoughts about his. It has been quite a ride, so far..

projects.title: Show HN: Keel – Give your agent a typed strategy language, not a trading account
projects.author: zferland
projects.summary: I’ve been using AI agents to build systematic strategies on Hyperliquid for over a year, and slowly built up a reliable system to represent, test and deploy strategies. Typically there are a few options 1) llm in the execution loop, ie it makes decisions and trades, but that is slow, inconsistent and hard to audit 2) you have an agent write all the code, backtest etc, but it makes tons of subtle mistakes with time series data and diff timeframe etc, and is often not reusing bits. There are some ways to improve this of course with right frameworks and setups. But its still hard to be confident in its correctness and its hard for you to verify quickly. With Keel we built a small typed language (DSL) to represent strategies. It uses a well defined set of components to build a DAG of steps, it carries types and clocks. This allows agents to build these strategies with a really fast feedback loop as they can be quickly validated and many common errors avoided. In a DAG its also easy to inspect intermediate results. Valid strategies are fingerprinted and the exact same artifact runs in backtesting and live. These strategies are also much easier for humans to verify as they are self describing components, and mostly linear to read and reason about. Still trying to improve the space of how many types of different strategies can be represented in this and still trying to improve how well LLMs go from natural language to strategy. A lot of the improvements come from just giving the agents better and faster tools and faster feedback loops.

projects.title: Show HN: Breadcrumb, record everything on your mac + context manager for AI
projects.author: jv22222
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Justin. Breadcrumb records everything you do on your Mac (screen + meetings + AI transcripts + what you and your AI decided) and turns it into memory your AI can search. It's local and encrypted. You can also teach it rules by talking to it and it makes sure the right rules turn up in the right context. Works with Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / opencode. All of this is exposed to your AI as 30+ MCP tools (here's the definitions): https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp I started it in June because I wanted to understand what was going on with my AI dev work. Then it just kept growing as I jammed on it 10 hours a day for 3 months. I started by recording every screen so I could jump back to a moment and see what I'd been doing with the AI. Then I added MCP so the AI could search it. Then time tracking. Then meetings with transcripts and timestamped screenshots. After that I started feeding the data back in. At first it was just a few relevant memories in the prompt. Then I started adding rules and rules modules. Then I started recording the AI transcripts and all the other stuff the AI did (subagents, tools etc). I wanted a complete record so I could go back and see what the AI did and why. I found the more data the AI had the more useful it became. One example. I got off a zoom call with the team at the day job and said: "Review the meeting I just had, find all the bugs we discussed, and create JIRA tickets with screenshots." It read the transcript. Found every bug we mentioned, pulled the screens from the screen timeline, spun up my local server, diagnosed each bug, reviewed the code, created 14 tickets in JIRA with diagnosis and likely fixes, attached 12 screenshots as evidence, and created a nice Slack message to send to my colleagues. I never built a workflow for any of that. Claude had the meeting record, Breadcrumb tools, and rules I'd accumulated. It basically chained the steps together itself. My favorite thing about the system is observability of my own work as an AI developer. I can trace a bug all the way back to the first thing I said (or the first thing the AI did) that caused it. Then I can add a rule so it doesn't happen again. Anyway, my working system is simply Claude Desktop + Breadcrumb + Markdown. I find I don't need anything else. It's local software for one person. Local models for transcription and diarization. Data encrypted with SQLCipher and a passphrase. You can exclude any apps, websites, words and phrases. Breadcrumb itself only makes one network call which is a daily update check. (but of course your AI will use it and that is local or cloud depending on what you use). It runs cool about 12% of one core on average (M series mac has 8+). You can set it to just save OCR text or to save screenshots. If just OCR it's about 12mb day (a lot of telemetry, indexing etc). If you record screenshots on meetings it's about 120mb/hour (1 every 2 secs). It can also record screenshots of everything that's heavy at about 160mb/day. It does local classification/naming with ollama with Gemma 3 4B (2.5 GB). It's 100% free. There's no account you can just download and start using it. I'll monetize it via E2EE cloud sync and team sync. It's open beta. Just one developer working on it. Requires 16GB+ M Series Mac. Thanks for reading! https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb (homepage) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/download (direct download) https://innerloop.works/breadcrumb/mcp (mcp definition)

projects.title: Show HN: Web search engine built from the CommonCrawl corpus
projects.author: xoredev
projects.summary: Hello HN, I'm building an alternative web search engine. You can try the demo here: https://search.xorsoft.dev/ My goal was to reach 1% of Google's index. This is 4 billion pages across 33.5 million domains. I was inspired by the earlier attempts shared here: "Building a web search engine from scratch with 3B neural embeddings" [1] and "Crawling a billion web pages in just over 24 hours" [2]. I decided not to replicate them and instead used CommonCrawl corpus, built a pipeline, and threw the results into a classic full-text search index. First, I got my hands on a dedicated Hetzner server with 4x10TB HDDs. It allowed me to crunch CommonCrawl data and stay within my hobby budget. The backend is served from a similar "home-grade" server but with NVMe disks instead. The compressed index weighs just over 2TB because I cap content length at 4KB per page (p50=2.9KB, p99=46KB) to fit it on disk. I picked Rust for my project. After years of big data engineering on the JVM, Rust felt like a breath of fresh air. I ended up not using any special data processing libraries - the pipeline is relatively straightforward and runs without crashes. As for full-text search, tantivy was an obvious choice. It took some time to get single query latency down to an acceptable ~350ms, although concurrent requests quickly max out disk t/p at 6.1GB/s and latency starts to climb. The search algorithm is primitive by modern standards: top 1,000 candidates are retrieved using BM25 (text relevance signal) and then reranked with PageRank [3]. Turns out you can fit the whole internet in a single server rack. The challenge here, of course, is to keep it up to date, especially if you don't have unlimited (crawl) budget. Right now I'm looking for funding or sponsorship to get extra hardware. That would allow me to scale the project and keep it free to use. I can also periodically dump the index on HuggingFace for research purposes. Any suggestions are welcome. projects.title: Show HN: Quiet – exploring when an AI assistant should intervene
projects.author: roger05
projects.summary: I’m Ruggiero, a CS student working on a research project about humanComputer interaction and AI. I built QUIET because I’ve been thinking about a problem with current AI interfaces: they usually either wait for an explicit prompt, or try to take over a task. I wanted to explore a different relationship between humans and AI: an assistant that can understand when to stay out of the way, when to point something out, when to teach, and when to act. I’ve built a small interactive demo of this idea. It’s obviously still very early, and I want to understand whether the interaction itself makes sense before trying to build the actual AI system behind it. The prototype is intentionally not AI-powered yet. The four examples are scripted so I can test the interaction itself before spending time building the underlying AI system. The idea is that the assistant can choose different levels/forms of intervention: * stay silent * point at something * explain / teach * do the task The important question for me isn’t whether an AI can perform these actions. Current systems can already do many of them. I’m trying to understand whether an assistant that decides when and how much to intervene is actually useful. I’d particularly like feedback on: * Did the interventions feel helpful or annoying? * Would you want an assistant to behave this way? * When would you prefer it to teach you rather than do something for you? * Does this interaction model make sense even without the AI being there yet? I started working on this because I feel there is an increasing gap between what computers/AI are capable of and what users actually understand and can make use of. At the same time, AI systems are becoming increasingly capable of explaining and performing tasks for us. I’m interested in whether the interface itself should evolve to bridge that gap. Demo: https://quiet-hci.pages.dev I’d really appreciate any criticism, especially if you think the interaction model doesn’t make sense. projects.title: Show HN: Silta: family assistant on Matrix with continuity across context limits
projects.author: dmitry-markin
projects.summary: Silta is a self-hosted assistant serving multiple users from a single Matrix account, used by me, family, and close friends for the last three weeks. It runs on Claude Code with each person using their own Claude subscription. Silta answers everyday questions, conducts web research (presenting the results as PDFs), performs scheduled tasks to monitor/research something and notify you if needed. It uses a deliberate handoff & compaction procedure, writing the compaction summary itself with a custom prompt, so the thread of the conversation and its picture of the user is preserved across context limits. As it turned out, the assistant accessible in a continuous chat (contrary to ChatGPT / Claude Web sessions) builds up better context about you and your tasks, and provides more relevant answers and help. It runs on Claude Code as the only allowed way to use a personal Claude subscription. Using Claude Code also spares me developing a harness, at the cost of tracking changes as new versions of Claude Code are released. The assistant itself (the daemon, the channel plugin, the supervisor, and the deployment) is open-source, while the model and the harness are Anthropic's and proprietary. Silta is deployed to a dedicated VM with separate Linux users per session and systemd hardening, protecting sessions from each other. Claude Code's bubblewrap sandbox is used to protect the Claude credential and the harness's state from the agent. This does not protect from prompt injections coming from search results and potentially leaking user data. Matrix E2EE protects the conversation from a Matrix server operator, but everything in the context is of course sent to the model provider. Private content is never logged, and the operator is expected to respect the privacy and not read the session transcripts on disk. Additionally, it is recommended to use full-disk encryption and tell the users how their data is handled. Silta only works in its workspace with files explicitly shared by users in the chat. Giving it access to a user's own computer or services like email is not planned. Since Opus 5.5 has been released, it is possible to run a session on a $20 Claude Pro subscription. Before that, only Fable 5.1 was pleasant enough to talk to. When run on Anthropic API, a moderately used session extrapolates to $100-$150 per month, with each research run costing $6-$12. Silta is built with Claude Code and Silta itself. The design, review, deployment, and testing are mine.

Articles are clustered using cloudflare's vector store, and related articles are also recommended with that. I have no doubt this will work even better with tech news, but there are plenty of alternatives out there, so I'm not going to indulge myself further. My takeaway is that Jev for content tagging is great so far. And edtech is kinda fun to keep up with. projects.title: Show HN: Autobox – Make your agents sandbox themselves
projects.author: freakynit
projects.summary: https://github.com/freakynit/autobox First of all: this is NOT for folks who are already using a sandbox. The guarantees provided by Autobox are weaker. This is rather for folks who "hesitate" to use sandboxes. Autobox is built around two observations I kept making over past one year of seeing sandbox launches and their real-world usage: 1. There are many sandboxing options now, and they work well. But leaving a handful few, almost nobody uses them. The blocker isn't the technology, it's the setup friction — however small it looks on paper, it's enough that people skip it entirely. 2. LLMs mostly don't write harmful code or take destructive steps. They're not adversarial by default. Autobox bets on the second observation to remove the first. Instead of asking you to configure a sandbox, it's just there: every tool call carries its own permissions, and anything you don't explicitly allow is denied. Is it perfect? No - seatbelt filesystem rules are best-effort, and the strong isolation is the V8 path. Is it better than using no sandbox at all? Definitely yes. This is also for M-series Macs only. --- Oh, and the best part: "copy_then_sync": Using APPFS `clonefile`, Autobox can hand your agent a full, "writable" copy of a repo instantly (1-2 ms). The agent gets something it can freely "destroy", but, your actual working tree is untouched. Your agent can then verify things, and of all looks okay, in one command sync the changes back to host within milliseconds.

projects.title: Show HN: Read the Odyssey in Greek while learning Greek

projects.summary: I made a way to (sort of) read the Odyssey in Greek without all those years of learning Greek first. I’ve had a deep interest in reading great literature in its original language since I studied Latin in High School, but wanted to find ways of reading real literature quickly. I’ve used this method myself to read books in several languages including Italian, German, Chinese, Japanese, and Greek. You still have to do the grammar and vocabulary study over time to really comprehend it, but this method has worked far better than all my previous attempts. The goal is to eventually be able just to read the language without any aids, but do that while reading real stuff the entire time. I’ve found that I go from needing help on everything, to learning individual words, to phrases, and then gradually I get to understanding whole sentences without looking anything up. Using a translation helps to keep me honest. I made a little demo of some lines from the Odyssey Book 1 to share the method and see if other people might find it useful. This is a special version that has a lot of explanation to see if something as difficult as Homeric Greek can be approached from 0. The interlinear translation and notes are AI generated though I made sure to ground them in real translations and existing grammatical tags. The commentary won't be as good as an actual Classical scholar's work and can be overly simplistic, but I'm hoping it's enough to get started. There are other versions that feature progressive grammar learning and identification as well as flashcards. If people are interested I'm happy to share the rest of the book or other texts I've made and read myself. I have the New Testament in Greek and then a bunch of other works in lots of ancient and modern languages.
