projects.title: Show HN: Jolt a decentralised content syndication network
projects.author: mercutio93
projects.summary: Hey HN i’m a platform engineer and my day job I mainly focus on kubernetes clusters and terraform with the occasional C#, Typescript when building services, so this could well be completely out of my depth. Jolt started as an experiment to see whether I could build my own network at all. I’ll also be honest that most of this code was agentically written. However the high level decisions and architecture were mine based on research, experimentation, trial and error. Canary testing was one of the consequences of that when you build this way you need something slapping your AI-driven confidence back to reality. This year I asked myself a question... Is it possible to have a platformless world? A world where no platform controls your data, mines it for ad targeting or bans you and takes away your audience with it. So I started working on that as a challenge just to see if it's possible... and I ended up with Jolt. Jolt is a p2p distributed content syndication network. Lol that's a mouthful, it's basically my solution to platformless content distribution. Someone can publish content using a cryptographic identity and others can discover that content. Apps can build on top of the network however they are decoupled from the audience or the account. Jolt achieves this with a daemon capability model kinda like how mobile apps ask for permissions, but for your identity and content. Apps don’t own your identity. They ask for a scoped session from the daemon (eg. "publish under /pastes/*") that you approve or decline. You can uninstall the app and you still keep the audience and the data. I'm gonna give you the jist of the work in this post and talk about the architecture in a comment but check out the RFC section on the github pages site if you want a deep dive. When I was building this the actual hardest part was not protocol design or crypto. Funny enough it was testing. LAN is deceptively simple and things just work; why? mDNS will find your peers instantly and make you feel cracked. Only to be humbled when you do a 3 node canary test to try to replicate the messy real world on a small scale. The 3 way canary tested my laptop on my home broadband, a relay in hetzner and my mac running on a mobile hotspot, finicky I know but that's all I had. I was trying to answer a hard question at v0: 2 nodes on different networks could communicate and more importantly behind actual NATs and how. The first attempt was via the relay so I knew that worked but I wasn’t really satisfied. I wanted direct communication and I spent about 2 days getting QUIC hole punching working for direct node to node communication. That being said im not fully sure it holds up in the wild, the realist developer in me doesn’t think so. One thing I'm sure about is that one canary test doesn’t cover all edge cases. I would need more nodes and people on the network telling me something is broken thats how I work lol and that's why I am posting this. You can jolt find here https://alexanderwanyoike.github.io/jolt/ So does this thing even work. Well I can happily say that I was able to build 2 applications on it Spoke ( https://alexanderwanyoike.github.io/spoke/ ) my attempt at building a platformless social network and Pastey ( https://alexanderwanyoike.github.io/pastey/ ) a simple pastebin like application when you want to send data to different places. Spoke is more maintained and I plan on getting Pastey to the same level of polish. They are still very early “hello world” prototypes. Otherwise if you wanna chat add me up on spoke fsjj2nvibhmztsw2w3klgkbjorqbze3qsi2tcwzbs5pepdigohiq.jolt ;)

projects.title: 【工具自荐】厌倦了繁杂的 App 套路？这是一个即开即用的极简睡眠时间计算器
projects.author: Thumbsai
projects.summary: 不知道你有没有过这种体验：明明睡足了八、九个小时，醒来整个人却像灌了铅一样沉重；反倒是有时候只睡了六个小时，睁眼时却莫名地清醒。 这其实与睡眠周期有关。科学研究表明，人类的睡眠由大约 90 分钟为一个单位的周期循环构成。在周期交替的轻度睡眠阶段醒来，会比在深度睡眠阶段被闹钟硬生生拽醒要轻松得多。为了解决这个虽然微小但每天都在折磨人的痛点，我做了这款极简工具——SleepCalculator。它没有任何花哨的监测硬件，也不推销付费课程，只做一件事：帮你算明白最合适的入睡和起床时间。 📌 基本功能 计算“现在睡，几点起”：当你熬完夜准备合上电脑时，点击即可。系统会自动加上平均 15 分钟的生理入睡缓冲，并列出 6 个契合完整睡眠周期的起床时间，供你定闹钟时参考。 计算“明天起，今晚几点睡”：输入明早的目标起床时间（如 6:30），系统会自动逆向倒推多个建议的入睡时间，帮你规划作息。 多档周期弹性建议：提供 3 到 6 个不同周期的选择（从短时间的临时小憩到 7.5 或 9 小时的完整睡眠），灵活适应不同时长的休息需求。 ⚡ 核心优势 零门槛，无干扰：市面上很多同类工具在积累用户后，往往会塞满杂乱的弹窗广告，或者强迫你注册账号。SleepCalculator.io 保持了极简的单页设计，无须注册登录，没有多余的信息负荷，即开即用。 更符合真实的生理缓冲：人不是机器，不可能躺下秒睡。工具在计算时特意预留了 15 分钟的入睡前置时间，让理论上的睡眠周期更贴合现实中人类的入睡习惯。 无焦虑的界面：这里没有长篇累牍的“健康报告”来增加你的睡眠焦虑，只有你需要的时间数据，适合在睡前已经十分疲惫的状态下闭眼使用。 👥 适用人群 作息不规律的独立创作者/程序员：经常被迫熬夜赶工，需要用有限的碎片时间精准补觉，避免第二天出现“脑雾”。 固定早起的上班族与学生：每天有固定的打卡时间，可以通过倒推入睡时刻，来降低每天早晨与闹钟纠缠的痛苦。 时差党或轮班工作者：在作息被打乱时，用它来科学安排不规律的睡眠，减少身体的疲惫感。 SleepCalculator算不上什么“能彻底解决失眠”的神器，它只是一个基于常识和生理规律的辅助计算器。如果你和我一样，厌倦了繁杂的 App 和各种付费套路，只是想要一个干净、安静的小工具，或许它能成为你浏览器收藏夹里一个实用的小角落。

projects.title: Show HN: SlickFast Deterministic Chart/Dash Renderer, No Browser(JSON → SVG/PNG)
projects.author: AlexRenders
projects.summary: SlickFast started 6 months ago, and evolved in a super backwards way. I was using lowfruits to look for good SEO keywords, I wanted to make a simple free tool to rank with SEO. I found some great keywords related to graphs/charts. I did research for optimizing for SEO. Turns out edge processing / using static HTML is super fast and lightweight, great for SEO. I made freepiechartmaker.com. I was really blown away by how fast the site was loading, and how lightweight all the processing was. The site renders changes on the fly, and is much much faster than other sites in the space. I started looking into the tech, pure math rendering, and I saw a lot of openings for what this tech can do. That's how SlickFast was made. SlickFast is a JSON input > pure javascript SVG Native render core > with PNG+SVG output. No headless chrome. No library calls. deterministic output. on my local machine(m1 max) it renders 140,000 svg charts a second. PNG @ ~50/sec at retina (scale-2) and ~145/sec at scale-1, single-core. (we have a benchmark mjs in our github repo) SlickFast can render 47 chart types. Any resolution, aspect ratio, any tile combination, easily deliverable anywhere, and made for agentic workflows. Our MCP is free and open source. Tiling allows complex dashboard creation. Each dashboard is only one render. SlickFast API serves URL endpoints. SlickFast is lightweight, we have a hero dashboard demo at slickfast.com/deck that is updating every 3 seconds. This is millions of renders, and the cost per month is less than $10. SlickFast was intended to be ready for agentic workflows, and visualizing agentic output as cheap and frictionless as possible. A benefit to the SlickFast deterministic pure math render core, is that edge servers will easily cache images. Millions of people can see a SlickFast endpoint, and only a few renders will actually be used, because the edge servers will happily cache our very small charts. SVG Native chart rendering provides for retina quality, at 50kb image sizes. Our favorite demo is LIVE GitHub dashboards, living right on the repo page. just put a SlickFast URL in your readme. You can see our living dashboard at github.com/slickfast/slickfast. We have made githubs templates for the public. you can easily add your own dashboard. https://github.com/SlickFast/github-dashboard-template SlickFast also has telegram deliverable templates. https://github.com/SlickFast/telegram-weather-template - if you go to the repo, the weather dash being sent via telegram, is on the repo as a live dashboard - Its updated everyday with a real weather report. Another great demo is our X.com NYC air quality index bot (@NYCAIRREPORT). Slickfast posts a AQI dash on X.com 3 times a day. With the new x API terms, each post is only about 2 cents. The cost on the slickfast side is basically nothing. Our free API tier currently provides 250 renders a month. Enough space for a few bots. Because slickfast was made for agentic use, an agentic was able to design the entire dash and inputs in only a few takes. AI Agents, can nearly one shot most tasks. One or two minor revisions is usually all it takes. Slickfast.com Github.com/slickfast/slickfast Slickfast is free and open source under AGPL license. I'm so delighted to provide some real value for free. We have a roadmap with some super cool things coming. Slickfast is very powerful for email, or tying to APIs. Thanks Everyone! I would love to hear your thoughts.

projects.summary: Title: Show HN: We built an open USB-C Power Delivery analyzer and programmable sink Hi HN! We’re Arbi, Marco, and Rob, and we built Dr. PD to make USB-C power problems easier to understand. It sits between a power source and device, captures and decodes their USB-PD negotiation, and correlates it with voltage and current measurements. It can also act as a programmable sink, with support for fixed supplies, PPS, AVS, and USB-PD 3.2 EPR up to 240 W. Commercial USB-PD analyzers are often priced beyond the reach of hobbyists and independent designers. We are on a mission to make high-quality test equipment more accessible. Dr. PD’s hardware, firmware, software, libraries, and documentation are all open source. Hardware and software are ready, and all the source and design files are available on our GitHub repo [1]. We’re also preparing to launch it through Crowd Supply [2], where you can also sign up to be notified when it becomes available. The host software runs locally in Chrome without drivers, accounts, or cloud services. Dr. PD also supports SCPI over USBTMC, Python and JavaScript libraries, capture export, and external oscilloscope synchronization. We have a full set of documentation [3], which includes a user guide, programming references, interactive schematics, and detailed hardware design notes. Happy to answer all your questions! You can also reach us at hello@t76.org. [1] https://github.com/T76-org/drpd [2] https://www.crowdsupply.com/t76-org/dr-pd [3] https://t76.org/drpd/docs

projects.title: 【开源自荐】model-verity：审计第三方 AI 服务声明真伪的 CLI + Web 工具（行为指纹验证）
projects.author: JESVN
projects.summary: 自荐一个开源项目。现在不少第三方 / 中转 AI 供应商会声称自己跑的是某个模型，但用户其实没法验证「到底是不是、稳不稳定」。model-verity 用行为指纹的方式做验证：对目标服务跑一组固定的 challenge，把它的 PAMELA 单 token 输出分布和版本化参考样本比对，给出一个 0–100 的综合可信评分（注意：这不是模型为真的概率、厂商认证或密码学来源证明）。 它同时提供 CLI 和本地 Web 界面，可以管理供应商、自建参考样本、查看历史验证记录并导出报告。 几个特点： 行为指纹验证：基于 PAMELA 单 token 输出分布，按行为一致性 / 请求质量 / 短时稳定性 / 可比性 / 参考强度五维加权，输出 0–100 综合可信评分 CLI + Web 双形态：一条命令起本地服务，浏览器里完成验证、比对、查看历史；也支持纯命令行 status --json 取结果 协议覆盖广：支持 OpenAI Chat Completions / Responses、Anthropic Messages 三种协议，不会在同一次运行中静默切换 adapter 内置研究参考库：随仓库附带 33 个主流厂商当前代模型参考（claude、openai、gemini、deepseek、kimi、qwen、glm、grok），数据来自 Zenodo（CC BY 4.0） 安全为本：供应商 Key 经 AES-256-GCM 加密保存、界面只显示掩码；默认只监听 127.0.0.1，公网部署建议走反向代理启用 HTTPS + 认证，默认拒绝私网 SSRF 安装： bash npm install -g model-verity model-verity start 也支持 Docker Compose 部署（镜像基于 Node 22，仓库自带 Dockerfile 与 docker-compose.yml）。 MIT 协议，欢迎提 issue / PR。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】拒绝几万字的文本垃圾：这是一个能帮视频快速“榨出”知识脑图的极简工具
projects.author: imagecolorpickerai
projects.summary: 相信许多人都经历过这种痛苦：为了在一期两小时的播客或公开课里找一个具体的知识点，不得不把进度条来回拉扯，拉得人心烦意乱；又或者开完漫长的视频会议，回头看着杂乱的笔记，完全抓不住重点。 我也是在无数次被冗长的视频折磨之后，决定推荐这个专门用来治愈这种效率焦虑的工具——TranscriptVideo。它不只是一个机械吐字的转录器，而是致力于把无序的音视频，变成真正能被检索、学习和利用的“结构化知识库”。 📌 基本功能 多源智能转录：支持 YouTube 链接、视频或音频直传。一键生成带精确时间戳与发言人识别的文本，让你告别从头到尾重播视频的低效操作。 AI 深度提炼与再创作：这是它最大的不同。不仅能转录，它还能一键将视频内容提炼为思维导图（Mind Map）、内容摘要（Summary）以及核心章节划分（Chapters）。 互动学习组件：系统能自动将视频核心要点转化为可供复习的闪卡（Flashcards）和自测测验（Quiz），直接在页面内检测自己的掌握情况。 双语对照翻译：支持跨语言翻译，让你在阅读译文的同时，依然能对照原视频的语音和原始语境进行交叉比对。 ⚡ 核心优势 从“转录”到“消化”的闭环：传统工具通常止步于生成一堆杂乱无章的文字块，让用户面对几万字依然无从下手。而它通过脑图和测验，帮你把碎片化的信息，真正沉淀到大脑里。 尊重上下文的“追溯感”：所有的脑图节点、提纲摘要都与视频时间戳深度绑定。阅读摘要时，点击任意要点就能直接跳转定位到原视频的对应秒数，绝不会脱离语境。 轻量即开即用：不需要你下载笨重的本地客户端，也不需要经历繁琐的注册流程，主打一个省心和效率。 👥 适用人群 重度自主学习者与学生：面对一两小时的线上讲座，无需重复观看。利用它生成的闪卡和脑图，能成倍缩短笔记整理和期末复习的时间。 独立内容创作者与播客主：需要将已发布的视频内容快速二次提炼，转化为图文帖子、博客提纲或章节时间戳，告别手动对轨的痛苦。 科研及媒体工作者：在需要对采访录音、长篇讨论进行内容检索与事实核对（Fact-checking）时，能通过关键词一键定位，快速获取关键素材。 说实话，任何自动化转录工具都无法在面对极度嘈杂的背景音或方言时做到绝对的完美，但与其让那些有价值的视频在收藏夹里“吃灰”，不如用 TranscriptVideo帮我们建立一个高效过滤和吸收信息的漏斗。希望它能帮你从无尽的进度条拉扯中解放出来。

I ended up with a templated, generic Viterbi decoder for convolutional codes that dispatches the decode at runtime depending on which instruction sets are available. For small rates and orders, the entire decode lives in registers. Larger codes work through memory but take advantage of some acceleration structures. I also spent some time building a tool to find optimal (max d_free) conv codes for a given rate and order. Of course, there are better mechanisms available today, but I'm happy to talk through anything I learned in the process.

projects.title: Show HN: Autonomous daily AI news briefing blog
projects.author: Komte
projects.summary: I like keeping myself in the loop of AI progress, and with an amount of things that are happening in the industry it has been quite a challenge. Yes there are plenty of AI newsletters and news-sources, including HN itself. However, all of those require significant time commitment. I was looking for something in a 5-minute-morning-briefing format, so I built it myself. Idea is pretty simple - every morning a pipeline is launched by cron on my raspberry pi. It crawls a few news sources (HN, reddit, tech crunch etc.) , aggregates, deduplicates and rates the news based on importance, then writes a blog posts with an overview and publishes it on the blog. This lets me quickly get up-to-speed and follow links for topics I want to explore in-depth. I also included key feedback from the community discussion which turned out to add a bit of "flavor" for otherwise plain news reading. I also added a podcast and newsletter format; I myself prefer to read it directly on the website but occasionally I can give it a listen instead if I'm for example traveling somewhere. It turned out pretty great if you ask me. After all, isn't this what AI is good at - summarizing text, and presenting it in a slightly different format?

projects.title: Show HN: Denorm – Declarative derived columns (Postgres)
projects.author: KenPainter
projects.summary: Denorm solves my own long-standing pain points with biz logic and the DB, providing a declarative DSL in which derived columns are part of the schema. Data moves along foreign keys: down from parent to child, aggregate from child to parent, and of course within rows. Can also generate parents and children along the foreign key. The README example: table us_states column state_code char(2) primary key column state_name varchar(20) column children_count integer count child_table table child_table column child_id serial primary key fk us_states references us_states pushes child_table column state_code is us_states.state_code column state_name sync us_states.state_name Denorm colocation of external values with derived values offers very high compression of logic definitions. It's a "pay me now" trade. The write is more expensive in exchange for simpler modeling, simpler reads and writes, simpler stack. The builder traps cycles, so we get termination. Builds are idempotent and additive, any-state to current. Ranged foreign keys are first class citizens (not just time series). Derived values are not subvertible. Race conditions and deadlocks eliminated (*except generating children can produce deadlocks the client must handle). If you already have Postgres installed, you can get something usable in 10-20 minutes following the README.

projects.title: Show HN: Guide AI coding agents on how to use libraries securely
projects.author: hajipour
projects.summary: Hi HN, TL;DR: AI Code Security Cards give coding agents library- and version-specific guidance to generate safer code. AI coding agents can generate working code, but they often lack library- and version-specific security knowledge. We've developed AI Code Security Cards, an open-source security knowledge layer, to provide that missing context. The project is related to my PhD, in which I focused on the security of LLM-generated code. During my research, I studied how code generation models behave, how they introduce security issues, and how we can guide them toward generating safer code. My research [1] and several other studies [2–4] show that at least 40% of code generated by state-of-the-art models contains one or more security issues. Similar problems also affect AI coding agents. One reason is that these models often lack sufficient library-specific security knowledge in their context. They may not know which configurations are unsafe, which validation steps are required, or what security-related behavior has changed between library versions. AI Code Security Cards provide practical, version-specific security guidance for open-source libraries. For example, the Django security cards can guide an AI agent on how to implement authentication and authorization securely. The easiest way to use the cards is to install the AI skill provided in the repository (And in the integration page: https://securitycards.rewarelabs.com/integration/ ). You can also download them and add them directly to your AI agent’s rules or instructions. We’d be glad to hear your feedback, especially on where these cards would be most useful in your workflow, which libraries we should support next, and whether you’ve encountered similar security issues caused by missing context. Website: https://securitycards.rewarelabs.com/ GitHub Repository: https://github.com/Reware-Labs/securitycards References [1] Hajipour, Hossein, et al. “CodeLMSec Benchmark: Systematically Evaluating and Finding Security Vulnerabilities in Black-Box Code Language Models.” 2024 IEEE Conference on Secure and Trustworthy Machine Learning (SaTML), IEEE, 2024, pp. 684–709. https://doi.org/10.1109/SaTML59370.2024.00040 . [2] Pearce, Hammond, et al. “Asleep at the Keyboard? Assessing the Security of GitHub Copilot’s Code Contributions.” Communications of the ACM, vol. 68, no. 2, 2025, pp. 96–105. https://doi.org/10.1145/3610721 . [3] Vero, Mark, et al. “BaxBench: Can LLMs Generate Correct and Secure Backends?” arXiv, 2025, https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2502.11844 . [4] von Arx, Tobias, et al. “AutoBaxBuilder: Bootstrapping Code Security Benchmarking.” arXiv, 2025, https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2512.21132 .

projects.title: Show HN: FutureSearch, AI forecasting you can verify
projects.author: ddp26
projects.summary: *Title:* Show HN: FutureSearch, AI forecasting you can verify AI forecasting is now approximately superhuman. Today, FutureSearch is exiting our long public beta and launching. We started FutureSearch in August 2023. (We’re the original AI forecasting company, at least in a Tetlock-ian, “forecast anything” sense.) We’re currently #1 of 194 in the most competitive AI forecasting tournament [1], and we score above the #3 and #2 human forecasters in the premier mixed human-bot tournaments [2]. Many people on HN seem to equate forecasting with prediction markets and finance. FutureSearch is not a financial tool, in the same way that “deep research” is not a financial tool. Yes, we do evaluate our forecaster on prediction markets [3]. But forecasting is about being as accurate about the future as possible, and the real game is in forecasting scientific progress, geopolitics, and the future of humanity. Our founding team came from Metaculus, where we pushed human forecasting to the limit on questions like when AGI would arrive. At. FutureSearch, we co-authored the AI 2027 timeline forecast, where we predicted superhuman coding and research would come around 2032, longer than the other authors, but still shorter than skeptics [4]. Thousands of people used the FutureSearch beta and ran >10k high-effort forecasts, on all sorts of diverse topics. Ask it anything about the future. We now support decision forecasts too: “If I do X, will I achieve this outcome?” Forecasting, as a capability, is useful even at the level of expert human crowds. But we predict that we will soon have strongly superhuman forecasting. People who bet against AI capability trend lines tend to lose, and the trend line in AI forecast accuracy tells a pretty clear story [5]. There’s no reason to think the best human forecasters have figured out everything predictable about the world. There’s a lot more signal to be found. And if you’re skeptical, try it. We’ve seen our fair share of exaggerated claims about AI forecasting accuracy [6]. So part of the reason we made the free tier give a few of our highest effort forecasters free is to let anyone verify the quality. [1] https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/summer-futureeval-2026/ [2] evals.futuresearch.ai [3] markets.futuresearch.ai [4] https://ai-2027.com/research/timelines-forecast [5] https://www.astralcodexten.com/p/the-ai-superforecasters-are... [6] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/uGkRcHqatmPkvpGLq/contra-pap...

projects.title: [开源自荐] 基于 Spring AI 的 ERP 智能助手
projects.author: ly1836
projects.summary: 这是一个基于 Spring AI 2.0 和 Spring Boot 4 构建的制造业 ERP 智能助手，集成 RAG、39 个业务查询 Tool、会话记忆、多租户隔离、调用追踪、计费和图表生成。项目提供中英文文档、演示数据与 Docker Compose，适合 Java 开发者学习企业 AI 应用的完整落地方式。 亮点 不只是简单的聊天或文档问答 Demo，而是一个可以直接运行的完整 ERP AI 应用，包含前端、后端、数据库、演示数据和 Docker 部署。 内置销售、采购、生产、质检、库存、财务、售后和委外 8 个 ERP 模块，共 39 个业务查询 Tool。 支持运行时配置动态数据库 Tool，并通过只读 SELECT、绑定参数、结果行数限制和租户条件注入降低 SQL 风险。 RAG 使用 PostgreSQL、PgVector 和本地 ONNX Embedding 模型，支持导入 PDF、Word、Excel 和 TXT 文档。 图表不是直接执行大模型生成的 ECharts 配置，而是由大模型选择类型，后端根据真实 Tool 结果生成可信 ChartSpec，目前支持 23 种图表。 支持 DeepSeek、通义千问和 Google Gemini，并包含 JDBC 会话记忆、SSE 流式响应、Tool 调用追踪和 Token 计费。 提供中英文 README、Apache-2.0 License、Docker Compose、初始化演示数据和动态 GIF，方便 Java 开发者学习和二次开发。

projects.title: 【APP自荐】vPlayer HiFi — 把 iOS 设备化身准专业 HiFi 播放器
projects.author: shanleiguang
projects.summary: 缘起 记得准备高考的那段时间，每天除了必要的锻炼，其他精力基本全都用来复习，唯一的放松，就是在晚饭时刻，当母亲把做好的饭菜端到我的书桌上后，我便合上书本，一边吃饭，一边打开练习英语听力的磁带机，随手放一盘自己喜欢的磁带。也许是唐朝的《梦回唐朝》，也许是黑豹的《无地自容》（《黑豹I》），或者是郑钧的《回到拉萨》，还有老狼的《恋恋风尘》。在那个白衣飘飘的年代，同学们会互相借磁带听，女生还会把喜欢的歌词手抄到带着花边的本子上，叫做歌词本。上了大学，在1999年的某一天，我在校门口斜对面的汉唐书店偶然买了盘一个叫做朴树的年轻人发行的专辑《我去2000年》，回到宿舍，同学们还都不知道这人是谁呢。后来他发行了第二张专辑《生如夏花》，我依然记得曾给某人在电话里清唱这张专辑里的《我爱你，再见》，而她人在电话那头早已哭的稀里哗啦。大学四年一晃而过，毕业季的旧货市场上，有个低年级的漂亮女生要打包全收我的那些旧磁带和杂志，我仔细地挑出了这盘《我去2000年》，连同在音乐学院、外语学院外打卡带地摊收的一套红、蓝、黑封面的披头士和当年一本叫做 Music Heaven 音乐期刊里带的那些极具风格化的欧美乐队歌手合集的磁带一起背回了家，直到现在，它们还安静的躺在我书柜的角落里，嗯，丢不走的行李，是我不变的心。上班后第一个月工资，我拿出大部分买了台蓝色的 Sony CD 便携播放器和森海塞尔 PX500 耳机，认认真真的煲够了一百小时，那时候经常光顾本地一家特色 CD 小卖店，店里全是复刻的国外经典 CD，平克弗洛伊德、披头士、大门、皇后、老鹰、恐怖海峡、涅槃等等，于此同时，互联网 P2P 开始有了萌芽，于是各种音乐专辑下载了一堆一堆，而电脑上的音乐播放器用过不少，比如 Winamp、Foobar2000、Audivana、HQplayer，还有特别小众的 BugHead。就这样，一转眼好多年过去了，现在的我更多是用手机听歌，不知不觉也已经成为 Apple Music 订阅用户好多年。就在最近，我开始学习 iOS应用开发，涌入脑海的第一个想法，就是开发一款能够运行在新老 iPhone、iPad 上的 HiFi 播放器，让家中 NAS、移动硬盘上那些之前认真下载、分门别类整理却沉默无言了许久的音频文件再次复活起来，于是，vPlayer HiFi，一款 iOS 上追求纯粹音质的 HiFi 播放器就这样诞生了。 命名 vPlayer 便是 Very Pure Layer 的简写，但这也的确反应了这款 App 的设计理念，就是希望把音频处理过程用分层方式直观的展现出来，让用户能够清楚的看到0、1组成的数字文件是怎么一步步转化成最终能够听到的波形数据，同时每一层又都可以单独启停或调整参数，可以方便地对比听感带来的轻微差别，从而找到那组最讨好自己耳朵的组合。巧合的是，我平时喜欢听古典弦乐，所以给它选了张小提琴作为 App 图标，而小提琴的英文也恰是字母 v 打头。 优缺点 在进行功能性介绍之前，先说说它优点和短板。优点包括： 它采用 Apple iOS 开发框架，能够同时支持 iPhone 和 iPad，未来还可以很方便的向MacOS、tvOS 平台移植。在用户管理方面，一个 Apple ID 账号的一次订购就能实现跨设备的统一认证和鉴权。 现代 iPhone 的硬件处理能力已经非常强大，拿两三年前的 iPhone15Promax 来说，它拥有 8G 统一内存（实测单一应用最多可用到 3G 左右）和最低 256G 存储容量（一张 CD 按照 500MB 计算，也可以轻松存储几十张），即便是运行本地离线量化 AI 模型也完全没有问题（详见我另一个App—锦囊AI ）。单从音频解码角度看，其实并不需要太大处理能力，实践证明，只要做好精细的资源分配回收，即便是2014年左右的 iPhone7，照样可以轻松实现 DSD 解码重播。 它可以通过 Airplay 协议方便的连接苹果生态，比如 Studio Display、AppleTV 等。 它能让你淘汰的老旧 iPhone、iPad 变废为宝。vPlayer HiFi 还有一个未上架的仅保留核心功能的版本，能够支持 iPhone7~X 的老iPhone，甚至我还为乔布斯时代的 iPhone4 移植了一个自用的 Jailbreak 版本，当 3.5mm 耳机口外接上更加古早的电子管收音机，听张人声爵士或者小提琴奏鸣曲，那情绪价值绝对是满满的。 相对的，它的短板也是明显的： iPhone、iPad 自带的 DAC 只支持44.1kHz和48kHz 解码率，这对于 HiFi 显然是不够的。如果音频原始码率是 96kHz 或是经 DSD2PCM 后的 176.4kHz 和 352.8kHz，又或者原始的44.1kHz 经软件 SRC、FIR 重采样至更高采样率后，一旦选择经过 iPhone、iPad 自身 DAC 解码重播，依然会重采样回落到 44.1kHz 或 48kHz。 这正是 vPlayer HiFi App与专业 HiFi 硬件播放器的最大区别，它只是一款运行在 iOS 上的应用软件，虽然 iPhone、iPad 的软件运行环境、CPU内存等基础硬件能力足够胜任对音源的处理，但其内置 DAC 解码重播的确是 HiFi 的短板。解决方案其实也很简单，连接外置 DAC 作为纯粹数播节点就可以了。然而，即便是使用 iPhone、iPad 的内置 DAC 播放，你也能清晰感受到 vPlayer HiFi 带来听感的明显提升。 主要功能 可视化信号链：信号处理以节点路径方式呈现DSD · MEM · SRC ⊕ FIR · EQ · DITH。点任意节点即可进入对应设置面板——切换 DSD 滤波器、设置 MEM 内存预分配空间、选择 SRC 算法、调整 FIR 参数、微调 EQ等。 Bit‑Perfect：采用定制化的 AudioUnit 音频处理管线与内、外部 DAC 对接，精确匹配音源原始采样率，确保 iOS 系统不介入、不重采样、零染指。 Native DSD Playback：支持常见音源格式 MP3 、AIFF、M4A（AAC）、WAV、FLAC外，还支持 DSD（DSF、DFF） 解码，提供多种 DSD FIR 降采样滤波器（陡峭 / 平缓 / 宽带宽），输出采样率包括 176.4kHz 和 352.8kHz，保留 DSD 原生特质。更支持SACD‑R ISO 镜像解析，内置原生 Scarlet Book TOC 解析器可直接解析 SACD‑R 的 ISO 镜像文件，形成音轨目录，并自动提取单音轨独立 DSD 文件点播。 Memory Playback：得益于 iPhone、iPad 的大内存，可将整首曲目一次全部载入预热后的专属内存缓冲区再重播，足以容纳一整张 CD Wav 文件或一首高码率 DSD 文件，从而彻底消除实时文件读写 I/O 带来的时基抖动（Jitter），让声音背景更纯净。虽然技术上有玄学成分在里面，但实际听感确有比较明显的改善。 多相 SRC + FIR 升频：提供 6 种采样率转换算法（从线性到 Sinc‑512 抽头），均采用 Kaiser 窗多相重采样。独立 FIR 升频支持 2× / 4× / 8× 倍率，抽头数可选（31 / 63 / 127），并可切换为同态最小相位模式。 10 段图形均衡器EQ：每段 ±12 dB 手动调节，并配有频段参考指南。响应瞬时、零延迟，可从信号链工具栏一键开启或关闭。内置 638 款 AutoEq 耳机预设，直接加载来自 oratory1990 测量数据库的固定频段 EQ 校正曲线，选择耳机品牌与型号后，即可一键应用，同时自动计算前置增益（Preamp），防止削波失真。 本地文件播放：通过 Finder 或 iTunes 将专辑文件夹拖放至 App 的共享目录，下拉即可刷新，左滑也可删除。 网络文件播放：支持局域网内 Samba 网络存储服务接入，采用边下载、边缓存、再播放的保守策略，完全避免网络抖动对播放质量的影响。特别针对 SACD-R ISO 大型文件（一般在 3G 左右），实现了单音轨 DSD 文件提取，从而大大缩短网络下载等待时长。对于喜欢的专辑，又可以左滑下载到 iPhone 本地。 双主题：提供“暗色”与“银色”两套界面风格，点击 vPlayer 标题即可轻松切换。 Lab 音频实验室：简易Room EQ 测量流程：两部 iPhone 协同开展，一部连接到房间音响系统并运行本 App 播放一段 20Hz 至 20kHz 的内置测量文件（务必提前带好耳塞），同时在听位头部位置，用另一部 iPhone 自带的录音 App 进行记录（提前打开高保真录音选项），最后将这段录音 Airdrop 到前一部 iPhone，App 加载后会自动对照原始测量文件，针对性的计算当前房间的 EQ 参数建议并可在 EQ 面板选择性启用。其精准度取决于第二台 iPhone 的录音精度，如换作高质量的便携录音设备参照性会更强。它主要是提供一种折衷的测量方法，在不改变现实听音环境基础上，可以明显改善低频污染。Shazam 歌曲识别：集成 Apple ShazamKit，轻点即可识别正在播放的音乐，获取专辑封面、风格、歌手信息。音乐绘画（Music Painting）：内置生成式艺术引擎，每首曲目都会绘制出独特的视觉画面，可选择“星座”或“印象”两种风格。画作可保存至画廊，随时浏览回味。 获取方式 希望喜欢音乐的你能够喜欢这款纯粹但绝不简单的 HiFi 播放器，它的特点正如老狼《恋恋风尘》专辑插页里的一句话：一杯清水，一种声音。 GitHub vPlayer HiFi Project 使用 iOS 设备登录 Apple App Store，搜索 vPlayer HiFi 即可。vPlayer HiFi App

projects.author: JanYork
projects.summary: AI Agent 很擅长阅读文档和解决当前问题，但会话结束后，已经完成的调查和整理往往也随之消失。下次遇到相似任务时，它又要重新搜索、重新阅读、重新建立上下文。 LLM Wiki CLI（命令名为 lwc）尝试解决这个问题：让 Agent 把经过筛选的本地文档整理成一份能够长期维护、来源可追溯的 Wiki。 Agent 负责理解、综合和修订知识，LWC 负责保存原始来源、Wiki 页面、引用关系、页面链接、检索索引和修改历史。这样，Agent 完成的有效工作可以跨会话继续积累，而不是每次都从原始资料重新开始。 思想来源 项目基于 Andrej Karpathy 提出的 LLM Wiki 概念： 让 LLM 增量构建并持续维护一份互相关联的 Wiki，而不是每次查询时重新从原始文档拼装答案。 LWC 将这个概念实现为一个基于 Rust 和 SQLite 的本地命令行工具，并提供配套的 Agent Skill。 与普通 RAG 的区别 典型的 RAG 工作方式是： text 查询 → 检索原始片段 → 生成一次性答案 LWC 的工作方式是： text 任务 → 读取已有 Wiki 和原始来源 → Agent 完成推理 → 将值得复用的结论写回 Wiki 检索只是 LWC 的一项能力，它的核心产物是一份持续修订的 Wiki。来源、引用、页面关系、矛盾和历史都会被保留下来。 LWC 可以与 RAG 配合，但它本身不依赖 embedding 或向量数据库。 主要特点 本地优先：使用 Rust 和 SQLite，日常存储与检索不依赖云端服务、后台守护进程或数据库服务器。 来源可追溯：原始资料保存为不可变快照，Wiki 页面可以明确引用对应来源。 知识持续写回：Agent 可以在完成任务后创建或修订页面，让有效结论跨会话复用。 项目与全局记忆分离：支持项目级 .lwc/ 和用户级 ~/.lwc/，避免不同项目的知识混在一起。 中英文词法检索：基于 SQLite FTS5/BM25，支持中文、英文和混合技术术语。 Wiki 关系图：保存页面之间的链接和引用关系，可以查询相关页面及结构化证据。 Markdown 投影：SQLite 是规范数据源，同时可以生成供人工审阅或 Obsidian 使用的 Markdown Wiki。 安全维护：提供 lint、索引重建、压缩、检查点和恢复等命令。 面向 Agent 的接口：命令以结构化 JSON 返回结果，仓库还提供配套的 using-lwc Skill。 安装 bash curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL \ | sh 也可以通过 Cargo 从源码安装： bash cargo install --locked --git README 中还提供了一段完整配置提示词，可以直接交给 Agent，由它完成 CLI、Skill 和全局记忆的安装配置。 适用场景 LWC 目前定位为单机、单用户的 Agent 知识库，适合长期软件项目、技术文档整理、研究资料维护，以及任何需要让 AI Agent 跨会话保留项目知识的工作流。

projects.title: [开源推荐] GOTO：记得一点，就能找到
projects.author: longqiyua
projects.summary: GOTO 当前阶段已实现为 以单一搜索框为核心的 Android 本地应用搜索与智能启动工具。它试图解决的并不只是“更快搜索应用”，而是让用户在记不清名称、输错字符，甚至只记得用途的情况下，依然能够找到目标应用。 用户可以输入中文名、拼音、首字母、英文缩写、T9 数字、用途词或带有错字的模糊线索。GOTO 会结合精确匹配、拼音检索、模糊纠错、键盘距离、应用标签与使用行为，从多个维度召回候选并进行排序，让搜索不再依赖准确记忆和准确输入。 项目由四个边界清晰、彼此解耦，并可独立演进的核心模块构成。四者分别负责输入预联想、搜索与排序、知识与状态存储，以及主动情境决策，共同组成 GOTO 的本地智能启动体系。 1. GOTO Prethink：搜索开始前的可解释预联想层：负责在正式搜索前分析用户的原始输入，针对重复字符、字符交换、键盘误触、不完整前缀和相近拼写，生成少量带有置信度与解释信息的平行候选。例如，用户输入 ggooogoto 时，它可以联想到 goto；输入 chorme 时，可以生成 chrome 候选。Prethink 不会偷偷修改用户输入，原始查询始终保留最高权重，所有联想结果最终仍交由 GOTO Engine 统一匹配和排序。 模块同时提供 JavaScript、Kotlin 和 Rust 实现，并通过统一 API 契约保持跨平台行为一致。

projects.title: Show HN: Kota – Bring AI agent CLIs into the same room
projects.author: chriswunan
projects.summary: A couple months ago, I was tired of keep copy-paste across different Agent Chatbot tabs, feeling like a slave for AI sessions, so I created Kota for my own work. Kota was designed around a concept of Knights of the Round Table. It treats human as part of a project team, and - Runs on top of existing CLIs with existing logins, - Gives each agent a persisted, viewable and editable identity, instead of sessions - Has a file-based long-term memory, - Uses a self-managed skillset, - Works on separated worktrees as workspace, and - Chats directly with other agents in the room. I have been using Kota for my daily work, hobby projects, as personal life assistants and to improve Kota itself, sitting down or on the go. Starting this week, I found it has become the only AI tool I am using now. So I am very happy to release Kota as an open source project, hoping more people can share my joy of living and working with these little friends. In the released version, you can use some most popular CLIs with Kota, keep their configurations, and invite them as team members to sit around your project table. These now include Codex, Claude Code, Pi, OpenCode, Gemini (Antigravity CLI), Kimi Code is already under testing and will be released soon. Some other stuff I included in Kota to make it more comfortable to use: - Remote with Telegram bot - Auto worktree sync and conflict resolve handoff - Skillpool, skillset, global rules, project rules, all manageable - A human-agent shared drawing board - An old school, cross-project social BBS - A lite AI-powered shell - Agents can dream about you Some next step and points of interests: - Agent Organization Building and Training - Agent working style cross project transfer without project data. - How to measure agent identity as meta data for task routing. White paper: https://www.kota.place/docs/research/long-term-teammates/v1/

projects.title: Show HN: Project ESPAÑOL: Find level-appropriate Spanish-language poems
projects.author: us-merul
projects.summary: I made this application while taking Spanish lessons to find texts that used verb forms I was learning (present, past, future, subjunctive, etc.). First, I scraped ~10,000 Spanish-language poems from the web that are in the public domain. Then, I built a conjugation dictionary for the 550+ most common verbs, using rules to generate regular verbs, and scraping irregular verbs from the web. From this alone, you can identify which poems contain the most type of verbs you're trying to target. To take it further, I used a k-means clustering algorithm in Python to classify the poems into four difficulty levels based on verb form frequencies (poems with lots of verbs in subjunctive future perfect are more difficult than only present tense, for example). I first completed the project in December 2024, almost entirely by hand, using LLMs primarily to make an interactive Plotly Dash application. (I have a lot of experience with data visualization, especially ggplot2; that was my first time using LLMs to write in a new domain.) Last week, in one hour with Claude, I completely updated the front-end to Javascript and Plotly.js. I hope someone can find it useful. It might be the only way to answer questions like, "Which 19th-century Colombian poet used the most future tense verbs?" (Depending on the available corpus, of course.) If I were starting this from scratch today, I would use LLMs to generate the verb forms instead of creating the dictionary that I did. But I would still have the analysis of the poems be deterministic. I also would use LLMs to assess themes and topics as an additional filter. And, of course, extend to more languages :)

projects.title: Show HN: Book-skills – Agent Skills distilled from mgmt and programming books
projects.author: damianmartinezc
projects.summary: I've been experimenting with Claude Code skills and wondered whether they could be used to encode the frameworks from books I repeatedly apply at work. The result is book-skills, an open-source collection of Claude Code skills where each skill represents a book (The Lean Startup, High Output Management, The Pragmatic Programmer, etc.). The goal isn't to summarize books. It's to make their methodologies executable. For example, after installing the Lean Startup skill, asking Claude something like: > "How should I validate this idea before building it?" is enough for Claude to structure its response around Build-Measure-Learn, MVPs, validated learning, actionable metrics, and pivot/persevere decisions. There's no need to explicitly mention the book or ask Claude to use that framework. Each skill is just a `SKILL.md` file with: - a description containing the concepts that trigger the skill - the actionable ideas from the book - instructions describing how Claude should apply those ideas I'd love feedback on two things: 1. Is this a useful way of reusing methodologies you already rely on? 2. Which books would you turn into skills? Repository: https://github.com/DamiMartinez/book-skills

projects.title: PyTorch Neural Network Guide
projects.summary: A free beginner-friendly PyTorch tutorial that teaches how to build, train, and evaluate your first neural network from scratch. It explains tensors, datasets, neural network layers, training loops, loss functions, optimizers, and practical examples in simple language. Designed for students, developers, and anyone starting their AI and deep learning journey.
